## Questions and answers
**What does MakeBiz do in the UAE?**
MakeBiz Technologies is an IT integrator: we implement AI agents that take over routine in sales, finance, procurement and hiring, and automate business on Bitrix24 for companies in Dubai and across the Emirates, including WhatsApp, accounting integrations, licenses and BI analytics.
**Are you an official Bitrix24 partner?**
Yes, MakeBiz Technologies is an official Bitrix24 partner in the UAE: we implement and support portals and help with cloud and on-premise Bitrix24 licenses.
**How much does Bitrix24 implementation cost?**
Standard Bitrix24 CRM setup starts from AED 10,000. Work beyond the standard is charged at AED 200 per hour, with a fixed estimate after a short survey. The Bitrix24 license is paid separately.
**How much do AI agents cost?**
One agent on your process starts from AED 5,000, maintenance is 10% of the implementation cost per month. A demo on your process is free.
**Can you connect WhatsApp to Bitrix24?**
Yes. Connecting WhatsApp or another messenger costs AED 500, the provider subscription is paid separately. Every message creates a deal and lands in the client card.
**Do you work only in Dubai?**
We work with companies across all Emirates, meetings in Dubai or by video call. We speak English and Russian, documents and invoices in dirhams.
**Where do we start?**
Leave a request. We run a free diagnostic, find where requests and time are lost, and propose the first step with price and timeline.

## Questions and answers
**How much does Bitrix24 implementation cost in the UAE?**
Standard Bitrix24 CRM setup starts from AED 10,000. Anything more complex (several departments, accounting integrations, data migration, custom development) is charged at AED 200 per hour with a fixed estimate after a short survey. The Bitrix24 license is paid separately.
**How fast can the CRM be launched?**
Basic launch from 14 days. Accounting integrations, telephony and non-standard processes take longer, we name the timeline after the survey.
**Is the license included?**
No, the Bitrix24 license is paid separately at the vendor price. Cloud starts from AED 180 a month billed annually, we help pick the plan for your headcount.
**Do you handle VAT and UAE specifics?**
Yes. We set up AED currency, 5% VAT on invoices and products, free zone and mainland company details, the Saturday-Sunday weekend, and work in English, Russian and Arabic where needed.
**Cloud or on-premise Bitrix24?**
We work with both. Cloud is faster to launch, on-premise goes on your server when data must stay with you or deep customization is needed.
**What happens after launch?**
We train the team and stay on support with hour packages: from 5 hours a month for AED 1,250.

Title: WhatsApp in Bitrix24 for businesses in the UAE | MakeBiz

Bitrix24 · messengers
# WhatsApp and messengers in Bitrix24
In the UAE clients write on WhatsApp, not email. We connect the company number to the CRM: every conversation in the client card, management sees who replied and how fast
MakeBiz Technologies connects WhatsApp to Bitrix24 through the official WhatsApp Business Platform, plus Telegram, social media and website chat: a new message creates a lead or deal, assigns an owner, and the history stays with the company. Connection AED 500.
## What happens without integration
### Clients on personal phones
Each manager chats from their own number. When an employee leaves, their clients and all agreements leave too
### No reply, and nobody knows
A message came on Friday evening, the manager saw it on Monday. Management learns when the client has already bought elsewhere
### History lives in the chat
Prices, discounts and deadlines were agreed on WhatsApp, and the CRM is empty. The next manager starts from scratch
## How we connect
### Official WhatsApp Business Platform
The company number connects to the Meta API via a connector in the Bitrix24 Contact Center. We pick the provider by message volume and price
### Open channels
Conversations are distributed among managers in turn, by language or by business line. Reply time is visible, a chat can be handed over
### A lead or deal from the first message
A new number creates a lead or deal with the WhatsApp source, a returning client lands in their card
### After-hours auto reply
Considering UAE weekends and holidays, in English, Russian and Arabic where needed
### Reply speed control
If a message has no reply in 15 minutes, a notification goes to the manager
### Channel report
How many chats, how many without reply and how many became deals
## WhatsApp rules to know in advance
### The 24-hour window
You can reply in free text within 24 hours after the client's last message. When the window closes, you can write first only with a template approved by Meta: a reminder, order status, an invoice
### Templates and broadcasts
Template messages are paid, the provider sets the price. Broadcasts only to people who opted in, otherwise complaints grow and the number gets limited
## What we do
Connecting a channel is not enough, it has to be built into sales
- 1
### Number and provider
We choose the company number and API provider and pass Meta verification
- 2
### Open channels
Queue, distribution, working hours and auto replies
- 3
### CRM and robots
Chats linked to leads and deals, reply time control
- 4
### Templates and launch
Templates submitted for approval, team trained, we stay on support
## Contract and guarantees
What you get besides the work itself
### Under contract
Contract with MakeBiz Technologies FZE LLC, invoices in dirhams, payment to a UAE company account. We can send the draft contract before the call
### Fixed estimate
Standard work at list price, complex work after a short survey: you see the scope and price before we start
### Access and data stay yours
Portal, server and accounts belong to your company. We work under a separate account and close access at the end
### One team
Implementation, support, integrations and AI agents by one team, no need to gather contractors
## Questions and answers
**Can WhatsApp be connected to Bitrix24?**
Yes. We connect the company number through the official WhatsApp Business Platform from Meta and a connector in the Bitrix24 Contact Center. Conversations land in the deal card, managers reply right from the CRM.
**How much does it cost?**
Connecting WhatsApp or another messenger costs AED 500. The provider subscription and paid template messages are separate, we calculate the costs before connecting.
**Which channels do you connect?**
WhatsApp, Telegram, social media messages, website live chat and email. All conversations in one Bitrix24 window.
**Why not via the web version QR code?**
That connection is unofficial, with broadcasts and complaints the sales number can be blocked. For the main number we use only the official API.
**Will the history stay if a manager leaves?**
Yes, the whole history stays in the client card in Bitrix24, not on a personal phone.

## Questions and answers
**Which accounting systems do you integrate with Bitrix24?**
In the UAE most often Zoho Books, QuickBooks and Odoo, some companies use 1C. We also connect bank statements, warehouse and internal services via API.
**What data is exchanged?**
Clients and companies, products and prices, VAT invoices, payments and stock. The scope and direction of the exchange are defined in the survey.
**How much does integration cost?**
Integrating Bitrix24 with an accounting system starts from AED 10,000. The exact price depends on the system and exchange scope, the estimate is fixed after the survey.
**Is 5% VAT handled?**
Yes. Tax rates, company TRNs and VAT invoices pass between systems consistently, so accounting does not fix documents by hand.
**What if the exchange breaks after an update?**
We take the integration on support: we monitor the exchange and fix it within the hour package.

## Questions and answers
**How much does Bitrix24 cost in the UAE?**
Vendor prices from bitrix24.ae as of October 23, 2026, billed annually: Basic AED 180 a month, Standard AED 364, Professional AED 731, Enterprise from AED 1,465. There is a free plan for 1-2 users. The on-premise Business edition is AED 13,184 a year.
**What currency are the prices in?**
The vendor publishes UAE prices in US dollars. We show them in dirhams at 3.6725 with the dollar price next to it, the exact amount is fixed in the invoice.
**How much does annual billing save?**
Annual billing makes the monthly price of a cloud plan about 30% lower than monthly billing.
**Which plan should we choose?**
A sales team of up to 5 people is fine on Basic. A company of up to 50 people: Standard. For process automation and end-to-end analytics: Professional. Branches and hundreds of employees: Enterprise or on-premise.
**Cloud or on-premise?**
Cloud is faster to launch and needs no server. On-premise is chosen when data must stay in-house, deep code customization is needed or there are many users. Details on the on-premise Bitrix24 page.
**Will you help with renewal and plan changes?**
Yes, we remind you about renewal in advance and help move to a higher or lower plan without losing data.

Bitrix24 · on your server
# On-premise Bitrix24: implementation on your server
Data stays with you, the system adapts to any process and connects to internal services. We install, migrate, customize and support
MakeBiz Technologies implements on-premise Bitrix24 on a company server in the UAE: we pick the edition and server, deploy the system, migrate data from the cloud or another CRM, customize it for your processes, integrate with accounting systems and take it on support. ## When you need on-premise
If two or more of these apply, the cloud will feel tight
### Data only in-house
Security policy requires keeping clients and documents in your perimeter or in the UAE
### Code customization
Custom modules, non-standard entities, logic that an app cannot do
### Many internal systems
Your own ERP, accounting, telephony and services that need deep exchange
### Hundreds of employees
With many users an on-premise license costs less than a subscription
### Branches and holdings
Free zone and mainland companies, different entities and permissions in one system
### Control over updates
You decide when to update the system
## Cloud or on-premise
### Cloud
- Launch in a day, no server needed
- Updates and backups by Bitrix24
- Customization via apps and webhooks
- Monthly or annual subscription
### On-premise
- Your server or data center, data in your perimeter
- Code access and customization of any depth
- Direct integrations with internal systems
- Annual license, cheaper with a large team

## Questions and answers
**How is on-premise Bitrix24 different from cloud?**
On-premise runs on your server or in your data center: data stays with you, you get code access, can customize deeply and connect internal services. Cloud runs on Bitrix24 servers, it is faster to launch, but customization is limited to apps.
**How much does on-premise Bitrix24 cost?**
License at bitrix24.ae prices as of October 23, 2026: Business for 50 users AED 13,184 a year ($3,590), with options for 100, 250 and 500 users. Enterprise from 1,000 users AED 91,776 ($24,990). Implementation is charged at AED 200 per hour, the estimate is fixed after a survey.
**What server is needed?**
Your own physical server, a cloud virtual machine or a data center in the UAE. We size the configuration for your users, deploy the environment and set up backups.
**Can a cloud portal be moved to on-premise?**
Yes. We migrate CRM, tasks, users and files, rebuild what does not move automatically and check the data before switching the team.
**Who will update and maintain it?**
We can take it on support: updates, backups, monitoring, security and improvements. Packages from AED 1,250 a month.

Title: HAVAL case: speech analytics for a dealer network | MakeBiz

Case · Automotive
# HAVAL: speech analytics for a dealer network
We analyze dealership sales calls across Russia: the system checks over 300,000 minutes of conversation a month against 40+ criteria, escalates to a senior manager when quality drops below 70%, and rolls everything up into BI dashboards.
Automotive Sales and B2B BI and analytics AI agents
Result 300,000+ call minutes a month
Client HAVAL, a global carmaker
Region Russia
What we built speech analytics, BI dashboards and AI agents
Before hundreds of thousands of call minutes went unchecked
After 40+ criteria on every call and escalation on risk
## The task
HAVAL has a dealership network across Russia and a huge flow of sales calls, over 300,000 minutes of conversation a month even on a sample. Checking that volume by hand is impossible, spot checks covered a fraction of a percent, and off the shelf tools could not cope with such volumes and 40+ communication criteria. Script deviations and lost sales went unnoticed.
## What we did
We built speech analytics as a fully custom solution: it processes calls across the whole network and scores every conversation against 40+ criteria based on a checklist and scripts, handling over 300,000 minutes a month. AI agents flag weak calls: if a conversation drops below 70%, it is automatically escalated to a senior manager so the sale is not lost. We connected BI dashboards with deep analytics on how calls influence sales and tracking of deals after a call, NPS and feedback collection, and we give management ready summaries. The speech analytics, the agents and the dashboards are all custom development. On top of that, agents book customers into the service center, remind about scheduled maintenance and upsells, and act as account managers.
## The result
Now HAVAL sees how the whole network talks to customers, at a scale beyond manual review or off the shelf tools. Weak calls are caught and escalated in time, script compliance is measurable, and the link between a call and a sale is visible in dashboards rather than guessed.
speech analytics + agents + BI: 40+ criteria , auto escalation below 70%, dashboards.

Title: Apartico case: property rental across Russia in one CRM | MakeBiz

Case · Real estate
# Apartico: property rental across Russia in one CRM
We brought rental of apartments, serviced apartments, dachas and houses into one system: over a thousand objects across the country, auto posting of listings to Avito, Cian and other portals, an AI agent that qualifies enquiries and helps with booking, and speech analytics that watches politeness and empathy on calls.
Real estate Services Bitrix24 and CRM AI agents BI and analytics
Result 1,000+ properties in one CRM
Client Apartico, property rental
Region Russia
What we built CRM, AI agent, portal integrations, speech analytics, BI
Before listings, portals and enquiries handled by hand and apart
After posting, enquiries, bookings and analytics in one CRM
## The task
Apartico rents out apartments, serviced apartments, dachas and houses across Russia, with over a thousand objects. Listings have to be posted and kept current on many portals at once, enquiries pour in from Avito, Cian and other sites, from messengers and by phone, and then they have to be qualified, taken into booking, confirmed and followed up for feedback. While all of this was done by hand and in different places, listings and enquiries got lost, managers drowned in routine, and there was no single picture of objects, bookings and service quality.
## What we did
We rolled out a CRM for property rental and tied it to the whole external loop. We set up automatic posting of listings to Avito, Cian and other portals and a reverse feed: every enquiry from portals, the website, messengers and telephony lands straight in the CRM linked to its object. First response and qualification were taken over by an AI agent: it replies instantly, clarifies dates, parameters and budget, suggests suitable objects and passes hot enquiries to a manager. Managers run everything in the CRM, and the agent helps at every step: booking, booking confirmation and feedback collection after check in. We connected BI dashboards so the team sees its metrics by object, portal, enquiry and booking. Separately we deployed speech analytics: it processes operator and client calls and scores how friendly, polite and empathetic the staff are, to keep service at a high level. The solution works the same for every object type and across all regions of the country.
## The result
Now the whole rental business lives in one CRM: listings are published to portals automatically, enquiries from every source are collected and qualified by the agent, bookings, confirmations and feedback are run in the system, and management sees the metrics by object and portal in dashboards. speech analytics shows how the team talks to clients and keeps politeness and empathy under control. The same process works for a city apartment and a house in the countryside, across the whole country.
CRM + auto posting to portals + AI agent + speech analytics and BI across all objects.

## Questions and answers
**Which VPS do we need for Bitrix24?**
Cloud Bitrix24 needs no server. For on-premise Bitrix24 with 50 users a server with 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM and an NVMe disk is usually enough, for hundreds of users more. We size the configuration for your users and load.
**Are there servers in the UAE?**
Yes, some providers on the list offer UAE locations, marked UAE in the card. If data must stay in the country, we start with them.
**Do you resell servers?**
No. You buy the server from the provider directly, on your own account, and pay them. We help you choose, deploy and configure the system and can take the server on support.
**How much does server setup cost?**
Work is AED 200 per hour or within a support package from AED 1,250 a month. We give an estimate in hours before we start.
**Why are the links affiliate links?**
MakeBiz may receive a reward from the provider, your price does not change. The list and order are the same as in our catalogue servercalc.com.

Title: Bitrix24 vs HubSpot for a UAE company | MakeBiz

CRM comparison · UAE
# Bitrix24 vs HubSpot
Both are good systems. The difference is the pricing model, what is included and how many extra tools you end up buying around the CRM
The main difference for a UAE company: Bitrix24 is priced per company (Standard for up to 50 users is AED 364 a month billed annually, bitrix24.ae price), while HubSpot Sales Hub is priced per seat (Professional from $90 per seat a month plus a required $1,500 onboarding, hubspot.com prices as of October 23, 2026). The bigger the team, the bigger the gap. MakeBiz Technologies implements Bitrix24, setup from AED 10,000.
## When to choose which
Honestly, each system has its strength
### Bitrix24 fits
A team of 10 or more, you need tasks, documents, telephony and chats in one system, a predictable company-wide price and an on-premise option
### HubSpot fits
Marketing and content come first, the sales team is small, you rely on English-language marketing integrations and per-seat pricing is not a concern
## Side by side
Vendor data as of October 23, 2026. Features depend on the plan
| Point | Bitrix24 | HubSpot Sales Hub
| Pricing model | per company, plan by number of users | per seat
| Example price | Standard up to 50 users: AED 364 a month billed annually | Professional: from $90 per seat a month
| Required onboarding | none | $1,500 (Professional), $3,500 (Enterprise)
| Tasks, documents, chats | in one system | focus on CRM and marketing
| On-premise version | yes, from AED 13,184 a year | no, cloud only
| WhatsApp | via connectors, our setup AED 500 | via integrations
Bitrix24: bitrix24.ae, HubSpot: hubspot.com/pricing/sales, checked October 23, 2026. USD/AED 3.6725
### We will calculate the total cost for your team
Tell us the number of users and the features you need, we compare both systems over three years in AED
Get the comparison
## Example for 25 sales reps
Illustrative figures from vendor price lists as of October 23, 2026. Rate 3.6725
Bitrix24 Standard covers up to 50 users: AED 364 a month billed annually, about AED 4,370 a year for the whole company. HubSpot Sales Hub Professional: from $90 per seat a month, for 25 seats that is from $2,250 a month, about AED 8,260, plus a one-time $1,500 onboarding. Our Bitrix24 setup starts at AED 10,000. We will run the exact comparison for your team on a call

- 2

- 3
### Migration and check
We migrate and reconcile counts and amounts
- 4
### Training
We switch the team over and stay on support for the first weeks

CRM · artificial intelligence
# AI-powered CRM for UAE business
What AI does inside Bitrix24, what agents add and what it costs
An AI-powered CRM for a UAE company has two layers: the Bitrix24 assistant CoPilot transcribes calls, writes summaries and fills in deal fields, while MakeBiz AI agents reply to customers on WhatsApp and score calls. CRM setup from AED 10,000, one AI agent from AED 5,000, speech analytics from AED 1,000 a month. Prices as of November 11, 2026.
## What the Bitrix24 built-in AI does
Bitrix24 helpdesk, November 6, 2026
### Call transcript
Searchable text in the language of the call
### Call summary
The key points in the deal timeline
### Fields from the call
Empty fields are filled, filled ones only get a suggested change
### Script check
The call is scored against your sales script
### Follow-up activity
The next activity with a short call outcome
### Chat review
Chats in leads, deals, contacts and companies
## What an AI-powered CRM costs
Our work and the licence
| Work | Price | Terms
| Standard CRM setup | from AED 10,000 | up to 20 users, from 14 days

## Where built-in AI is not enough
### CoPilot in the record
Helps with one call or chat, within plan limits

The AI sales head replies on its own if the rep is silent for 15 minutes
### Every team call
Speech analytics scores every call, rep by rep

The difference is in our news on agents and rules
## Limits, plan and data
Regular Bitrix24 plans have monthly AI limits, Vibe+ plans do not (Bitrix24 blog, August 17, 2026). Agents reach a cloud portal through the REST API, which per the Bitrix24 documentation now comes with Vibe+ plans, not Essentials. CoPilot runs on third-party models such as OpenAI; if data must stay with you, we deploy agents on your server, including in the UAE. Plan prices: Bitrix24 licences

An illustration, not a case. 8 reps, leads from WhatsApp and calls. CRM setup AED 10,000 plus the AI sales head on the Start package for AED 5,000, who answers in the evening and at weekends. ## Bitrix24 plan and REST API
apidocs.bitrix24.com, checked November 11, 2026
Ongoing REST API access in the cloud now comes with Vibe+ plans, not Essentials. Existing subscriptions may keep access for a transition period, and a 15-day Professional Vibe+ trial is available for testing. The cloud limit is 2 requests per second with a burst of up to 50, on Enterprise 5 and 250. On-premise, your server sets the load. So we check the plan before the estimate and for heavy exchanges consider on-premise Bitrix24 ; see our news on cloud or own server
## How we work
- 1
### Review
What to connect, which data, which direction
- 2
### Map and estimate
Objects, fields, events, hours and price in AED
- 3
### Build and test
Test data first, then live data
- 4
### Launch and support
Exchange documentation, then a support package

Page: https://makebiztechnologies.com/en/journal/supplier-quote-comparison
Title: Comparing supplier quotes: criteria and a table | MakeBiz

Journal · Documents
# Comparing supplier quotes: criteria and a comparison table
Four suppliers sent four quotes in four different formats, and your buyer has to work out which one is actually cheaper. Here is a table template, the order to compare in, and how an AI agent builds the table from emails and files.
Compare supplier quotes line by line and on one basis: unit price excluding VAT in AED at a recorded exchange rate, delivery, lead time and stock, payment terms, minimum order, warranty and quote validity. Set the weights for each criterion before you open the quotes. The MakeBiz Technologies procurement agent builds this table from emails and files on its own: one agent is AED 5,000 one-off to implement, and the demo is free.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## Compare line items, not quote totals
A quote total is almost never comparable as it stands. One supplier priced nine items out of ten, another quoted per box instead of per piece, a third included delivery and a fourth did not. Put the totals side by side and the winner is whoever left something out.
So each row in the table is a line item from your request, and each column is a supplier. Before you open any replies, lock the item list, the quantities and the base unit: piece, kilo, metre. Every quote then drops into the same grid, and gaps show up straight away.
## Nine columns cover almost any purchase
For every item and every supplier, the same fields get filled in. This template is a good place to start:
| Column | What to record | How to normalise it
| Unit price | Price from the quote and the unit it refers to | Convert to the base unit of the request
| Currency and rate | Quote currency | Convert to AED at the rate on the comparison date, and record both
| VAT | Included, on top or not stated | Price excluding VAT, tax in its own column, "not stated" means a question to the supplier
| Delivery | Delivered to warehouse, ex-works, who pays freight | Add the delivery cost to the price or show it as a separate line
| Lead time and stock | Ex-stock in the UAE or made to order | Days from order to delivery
| Payment terms | Advance, credit terms, instalments | Advance share and credit period in days
| Minimum order | MOQ and pack multiples | Check your quantity meets it
| Warranty and returns | Period and conditions | One wording for all suppliers
| Quote validity | Date the price holds until | Do not compare an expired quote without reconfirmation
MakeBiz Technologies template. Add columns for your category: certificates, country of origin, after-sales service.
A word on currency and VAT: the standard UAE VAT rate is 5%, and if one quote includes it and another does not, that gap can easily outweigh the difference between two close offers. We covered four traps like this in our news piece on where money leaks when comparing suppliers .
## Set the weights before you open the quotes
Weights invented after the fact quietly bend towards the supplier someone already likes. So write them into the purchase record up front. A hypothetical set for consumables: price 50, lead time 20, payment terms 15, track record 15. For an urgent order you raise the lead time weight, for a large batch payment terms and minimum order matter more.
Scoring is simple: the supplier with the lowest price gets 10 points on price, the others get proportionally less. Lead time works the same way. The total is the sum of scores multiplied by the weights.
Track record comes from history, not gut feeling: how often a supplier missed a date, changed the price after quoting or went silent. You only have that data if purchasing runs in a CRM rather than in personal spreadsheets. How to set up the request process itself is in our guide to procurement automation .
### We build your quote comparison table
The procurement agent reads quotes from email and messengers and puts them on one basis. AED 5,000 one-off
Book a demo
## The agent builds the table from emails and files
Done by hand, it looks like this: the buyer opens every email, hunts for the price in a PDF, types it into Excel, converts boxes to pieces and hopes nothing was missed. The procurement agent does the same job by the rules you set:
- picks up quotes from email and messengers connected to the CRM
- reads PDFs, Excel files, scans and email text and maps the figures to request line items
- converts units and currency at your rate and separates VAT
- keeps the source of every value, the file and the spot in it, so it can be checked in one click
- flags missing items, unstated VAT, expired quotes and prices far from the item's history
If something is missing, the agent sends the supplier a clarifying question and waits for the answer. How AI reads documents and where it stops is covered in our guide to invoice and document recognition .
## The recommendation explains the choice, it does not make it
Once the table is complete, the agent scores it with your weights and writes a short note: why supplier B comes first, what the risk is with supplier A, which items to re-request from C. The buyer decides. If they pick someone other than the top scorer, the reason goes into the record in one line, so it can be found six months later.
The boundary is the same as in any agent work: it handles documents and numbers, while negotiation, exceptions and signatures stay with a person. More on how roles split between an agent, an automation rule and an employee on our AI in Bitrix24 page.
## Keep the table with the decision
A comparison saved in someone's personal file is gone by the next purchase. In a CRM the table stays in the record together with the original quotes, the chosen supplier and the reason. In Bitrix24 this is a purchasing smart process, see our Bitrix24 development page.
After a few months those records add up to a price history for every item and supplier. It reads well on a BI analytics dashboard: the Basic plan is AED 300 a month, with the first 14 days free. All prices are on our pricing page .
## A worked example: four quotes for consumables
A hypothetical company asks four suppliers to quote on ten items. The first has the lowest total, but two items are missing and VAT is not stated. The second quotes per box of 12. The third offers made to order with a long lead time. The fourth includes delivery to the warehouse. Once everything is on one basis, the first quote goes back for clarification, and the real choice is between the second and the fourth, settled by the lead time weight agreed in advance.
## Questions and answers
**How many suppliers should we compare per purchase?**
There is no fixed rule: for routine purchases three to five is common, for a large one-off order you ask more. What matters is that everyone gets the same specification and the same reply deadline.
**What if a supplier does not state VAT?**
Do not guess, ask in writing. Until they reply, mark the quote as incomplete, otherwise a 5% gap can make the choice for you.
**Can we compare quotes in Excel?**
Yes, if there is one template for all purchases and the table is kept with the decision. Problems start when every buyer has their own file and the price history leaves with the employee.
**How does the agent get supplier quotes?**
From email and messengers connected to the CRM. It reads PDFs, Excel files and email text, maps the figures to request line items and records the source of each value.
**How much does automated quote comparison cost?**
The procurement agent on the Start package is AED 5,000 one-off, with support at 10% of the implementation fee per month. We show the agent on your own process for free in 30 to 40 minutes.

Title: CRM for a small business in the UAE: needs and costs | MakeBiz

# CRM for a small business in the UAE: what you need and what it costs
A team of 5 to 10 people does not need a CRM for fancy reports. It needs one so that WhatsApp, website and phone enquiries stop slipping through. Here is the minimum to cover and what it costs in AED.
Most small businesses in the UAE are well served by cloud Bitrix24: Basic for 5 users costs AED 180 a month and Standard for 50 users AED 364 (billed annually, bitrix24.ae prices as of 23 October 2026). Standard CRM setup with MakeBiz Technologies starts at AED 10,000 and goes live from 14 days, and connecting WhatsApp is AED 500 plus the provider subscription.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## A small team needs one pipeline, not the whole platform
A company of 5 to 10 people has no analytics team and no appetite for a six-month project. Here a CRM does simple jobs: every enquiry lands in one place, has an owner, a next step and a chat history. When that works, the owner can see how much money is in the pipeline without chasing reps in a group chat.
The minimum to start with:
- one sales pipeline with 5 to 7 clear stages
- website, WhatsApp and phone enquiries going straight into the CRM
- tasks and reminders so no client waits days for a reply
- a client record with a +971 phone number, email and history
- access rights: reps see their own deals, the owner sees everything
Inventory, smart processes and advanced reports can wait until the team is used to the basics. Where Dubai companies usually start automating is covered in our news piece on first automation steps .
## Your Bitrix24 plan depends on headcount
For a small business the choice is usually between two cloud plans. The key difference is the user limit: Basic covers 5 people, so the day you hire a sixth, you move to Standard.
| | Basic | Standard
| Users | up to 5 | up to 50
| Price per month | AED 180 ($49) | AED 364 ($99)
| Over 12 months | AED 2,160 | AED 4,368
| Good fit for | A team of up to 5 with no hiring planned this year | A team of 6 to 10, or one about to grow
License prices billed annually, bitrix24.ae prices as of 23 October 2026, exchange rate 3.6725. Since November 2026 bitrix24.ae also offers the Vibe+ line, and cloud REST API access is only available there, so check the current plan before you buy.
More on the Bitrix24 licenses page, and a comparison for different team sizes in our guide on which plan to choose for 10, 25 or 50 users .
## WhatsApp is the first channel to connect
Customers in the UAE are quick to message on WhatsApp. If those chats live on reps' personal phones, you cannot see who said what, and when someone leaves, their clients leave with the phone.
That is why WhatsApp goes into the CRM early: a company number, open channels and a lead created from the first message. We connect it for AED 500, while the provider subscription and Meta message fees are paid separately. The scope is on the WhatsApp and messengers in Bitrix24 page, Meta pricing is in our news piece on WhatsApp Business costs in the UAE , and the case for the official channel over a browser connector is in our guide WhatsApp Business API or WhatsApp Web .
Your website is usually the second channel: a CRM form creates a lead with its source and UTM tags, and the rep gets a task right away. See our guide to Bitrix24 CRM forms .

## Launch simple, then add automation
A small business does not need a long project. A short loop works: launch a basic pipeline, use it for a month, collect the team's feedback, then add automation. The usual order:
- week one: pipeline, fields, client import from a spreadsheet, access rights
- week two: WhatsApp, website form, automation for tasks and reminders
- after launch: team training on your own portal and fixes based on feedback
A short session answers most first-month questions, see Bitrix24 training . If you expect frequent tweaks, a support plan is easier than a separate invoice for every small change.
## Three mistakes eat up the value of a CRM
- Buying a plan and never setting it up. An empty portal with no pipeline or channels becomes one more browser tab nobody opens
- Leaving WhatsApp on personal phones. Only part of your enquiries reach the CRM, so reports show half the picture
- Automating everything at once. Dozens of rules in week one confuse the team, start with tasks and reminders
Once the pipeline runs, the next step is often an AI agent. The AI sales manager agent replies to a client if a rep goes quiet and makes sure every deal has a next step. The Start package with one agent is AED 5,000 one-off, and a demo on your own process is free.
## A worked example: a fit-out company with 8 people
A hypothetical Dubai apartment fit-out company has an owner, 4 sales reps, 2 site supervisors and an office manager. Enquiries come through WhatsApp and the website, quotes go out from personal phones, and some clients drop off between the site visit and the contract.
The company takes Standard, because 8 users do not fit into Basic: AED 4,368 a year. A pipeline of enquiry, site visit, quote, contract, works and payment, plus WhatsApp and the website form, is estimated from the AED 10,000 standard setup plus AED 500 for the channel. A month later the owner sees every enquiry in one place and knows where each one is stuck.

Title: Sales forecasting from CRM data: how it works | MakeBiz

Journal · Analytics
# Sales forecasting from CRM data
A forecast based on gut feel misses actuals every month. If your CRM holds amounts, stages and dates, you can forecast from data and check it every week.
A CRM sales forecast combines the value of open deals, the probability of each stage based on past closes, and the payment date adjusted for your average sales cycle. In MakeBiz BI the monthly and quarterly forecast is part of the Standard plan at AED 700 a month, and the first 14 days are free.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## A forecast is built from three numbers: amount, probability and date
Every open deal in your CRM has an amount, a stage and an expected close date. Those three fields are what a forecast is made of. The amount tells you what you could earn. The probability tells you how likely it is. The date tells you which month the money lands in.
The simplest formula multiplies each deal amount by its stage probability and adds the results up by month: a weighted pipeline. A deal worth AED 40,000 at a stage with a 25% probability contributes AED 10,000 to the forecast. No single deal pays exactly that, but across many deals the errors cancel out.
The weak spot is data quality. A blank amount drops the deal out, and a close date that has said "tomorrow" for three months keeps the forecast sliding. So the data comes first, more on that below.
## Stage probability comes from history, not gut feel
In many portals stage probabilities were typed in during setup: 10, 30, 50, 90%. Those are guesses. A real probability comes from closed deals over the last 6 to 12 months: of all deals that reached a stage, how many ended up paying.
| Stage | Deals that reached it | Of those, paid | Probability
| New lead | 400 | 48 | 12%
| Qualified | 200 | 48 | 24%
| Quote sent | 120 | 48 | 40%
| Negotiating terms | 70 | 48 | 69%
| Invoice issued | 55 | 48 | 87%
A hypothetical example with made-up figures to show the calculation. Your probabilities are calculated from your own deals.
Recalculate probabilities every quarter and separately for each line of business. A repeat order and a first deal with a new client behave differently at the same stage, and so may separate free zone and mainland teams.
## The sales cycle moves the forecast between months
Reps set close dates optimistically, so the deal date is compared with the average cycle from each stage to payment. If deals at "Quote sent" typically close 35 days later and a rep has set a date one week out, the forecast uses the calculated date instead.
The second rule covers stalled deals. A deal that has been sitting at a stage two or three times longer than average is very unlikely to close on time. Those deals go onto a separate list for the sales manager and carry less weight in the forecast. You can hand stalled-deal control to the AI sales manager : the agent watches the pipeline, nudges the rep and alerts the manager if nothing happens.
### We build a sales forecast on your CRM
Stage probabilities from history, plan, forecast and actuals on one dashboard. Forecasting in BI from AED 700 a month, 14 days free
Talk about forecasting
## Run the weighted pipeline and the rep forecast side by side
Stage maths cannot know what the rep knows: the client has signed internally, but payment will clear after quarter end. That is why a rep forecast runs alongside the weighted pipeline. In Bitrix24 we add a deal field with three values:
- Commit : the deal will close this period and the rep stands behind it
- Upside : there is a real chance, but open questions remain
- Not this period : the deal is alive, but the money will come later
The sales director looks at both. If the rep forecast is far above the weighted pipeline, the team is overrating its deals; far below, and deals may be stuck. The weekly meeting turns to specific deals instead of impressions.
Calls are another source of truth. What a client says about timing and budget often never makes it into the deal record. Call speech analytics, from AED 1,000 a month for 5,000 minutes, helps you see it. Read more in our news on what gets lost between the call and the deal record and on the call analysis agent page.
## Clean CRM data comes before the forecast
A forecast inherits every error in your CRM. The minimum checklist before you start:
- Every open deal has an amount in AED and a close date
- Stages have exit criteria: what has to happen for a deal to move on
- No duplicate deals for the same client and the same need
- Lost deals are closed with a reason instead of lingering in the pipeline
- Deal amount and invoice amount are calculated the same way, with or without 5% VAT
We cover typical data problems in our guide on why CRM reports lie . If nobody has reviewed the portal in a while, start with a Bitrix24 audit . If you have no CRM yet, or the pipeline does not match how you actually sell, you need Bitrix24 setup first: the standard package starts at AED 10,000 and go-live takes from 14 days.
## Plan, forecast and actuals belong on one dashboard
A working forecast lives on a dashboard that refreshes itself. One screen, three lines by month: the sales plan, the weighted pipeline forecast and actual payments. Underneath, a table by rep and a list of the deals that carry the most weight in the forecast.
Actual payments are more reliable when they come from accounting rather than from the "Won" stage. We connect Bitrix24 to Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo from AED 10,000, see the integrations page . In MakeBiz BI analytics the monthly and quarterly forecast and stalled deals come with the Standard plan at AED 700 a month, sales plans come with Pro at AED 1,000, and accounting systems are connected to BI on request for an extra fee. The first 14 days are free. To connect ad spend to those payments, see our guide on end-to-end analytics .
## A worked example: a distributor with 20 sales reps
A hypothetical Sharjah distributor runs sales in Bitrix24, yet the director builds the monthly outlook in a spreadsheet by calling each rep, and actuals never match it.
First the team cleans up the pipeline: dead deals get closed, amounts and dates get filled in. Then stage probabilities are recalculated from a year of history, and deals get a rep forecast field. A month later the director sees plan, weighted pipeline and actuals on one screen and only discusses deals with gaps at the weekly meeting. What a project like this costs for you is set in a quote before work starts, and rates are on our pricing page .
## Questions and answers
**How do I calculate the probability of a deal stage?**
Take closed deals from the last 6 to 12 months and work out what share of deals that reached the stage ended up paying. That share is the probability, and it should be recalculated every quarter.
**What is a weighted pipeline?**
It is the total of all open deals, each multiplied by the probability of its stage. It shows expected revenue by month, allowing for the fact that some deals will not close.
**How much data do I need for a forecast?**
You need a history of closed deals, both won and lost, with amounts and dates. The more deals per period, the more stable the probabilities. With only a few deals, the rep forecast matters more than the maths.
**Can I build the forecast inside Bitrix24?**
Bitrix24 has basic pipeline reports. For plan, forecast and actual payments from accounting on one screen, a BI dashboard is more practical, and it refreshes automatically.
**How much does sales forecasting cost with MakeBiz?**
The monthly and quarterly forecast comes with the BI Standard plan at AED 700 a month, and sales plans with Pro at AED 1,000. If the CRM data needs cleaning first, that work is billed at AED 200 an hour against a quote agreed before we start.

Title: Sales call analysis: what to check and how to coach | MakeBiz

Journal · AI agents
# Sales call analysis: what to check and how to coach
Almost every CRM stores call recordings, yet few teams get much out of them: nobody has time to listen, and after listening it is not clear what to tell the rep. Call analysis works when you have criteria, numbers against them and a clear way to review.
Score a sales call by the stages of the conversation (opening, discovery, pitch, objections, next step) plus the rep's delivery. MakeBiz call speech analytics scores every call against your own script from AED 1,000 a month for 5,000 minutes, and the sales manager coaches one skill at a time using real moments from those calls.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## Call analysis starts with criteria, not with listening
If a manager listens to a call without a list of criteria, the score depends on their mood and on whether they liked the rep's voice. A month later those scores cannot be compared across people or over time.
So first you break the sales script into stages and write down what counts as done for each one. Not "good discovery", but "asked at least two open questions about the client's problem and played it back in their own words". The more specific the wording, the fewer arguments in the review. How a dropped conversation gets tied to a specific stage is covered in our news piece on where sales teams lose clients inside the call .
## Six blocks of criteria cover a typical sales call
The set below works for most phone sales, B2B and B2C. Trim it or extend it for your process, for example with a separate criterion for follow-up calls.
| Block | What we check | Red flag
| Opening | Introduced themselves, named the company and the reason for the call, checked it is a good time | The client asks who is calling
| Discovery | Open questions, the client's problem, timing, who makes the decision | Jumps to the pitch within a minute
| Pitch | Talks about value for the client's problem, not the product in general | A monologue with no questions
| Objections | Finds out what is behind the objection and answers the real concern | An argument, or an instant discount
| Next step | A specific agreement: date, action, channel | "I'll call you back" with no date
| Delivery | Pace, interruptions, the rep's share of talk time | The rep does nearly all the talking
MakeBiz Technologies baseline criteria, November 2026. The final list is agreed against your script.
The blocks do not carry equal weight. A missed greeting rarely costs a deal, while a call with no next step almost always ends in silence. So criteria get weights: discovery and the next step score more, delivery scores less. Agree the weights with the head of sales before the first report, or the numbers will be disputed.
## Read call scores by rep and by stage
An overall team average tells you very little. Two views are useful:
- by stage across the team. If almost everyone fails the next step, the problem is the script or the training, not individual people
- by rep on a single stage. If one rep keeps losing points on objections, that is the topic of their one-to-one
A third useful view is client questions and objections across all calls. Repeated questions show what to add to the script and the website, and repeated objections point to where the offer itself needs work. Much of this never makes it into the CRM, as we wrote in our news piece on what you hear on a call but never see in the deal .
### We score every call against your script
Criteria built around your process, scores by rep and stage, top objections. From AED 1,000 a month for 5,000 minutes
See it on our calls
## Coach one skill at a time
A common coaching mistake is listing everything that went wrong. The rep remembers one or two points and hears the rest as criticism. This order works:
- Pick one stage where the rep consistently scores low
- Find 2 or 3 calls where the mistake is obvious, and one where they got it right
- Listen to the clips together, starting with the good one
- Agree on one concrete action: which question to ask, which phrase to drop
- A week later, check the same criterion on new calls
A short session every week beats an hour-long meeting once a month: the rep has time to try one change and see it in their own numbers.
## Training is built from real call clips
Once calls are scored, you end up with a library: strong answers to common objections, good discovery questions, examples of a clean next step. That is material for new hires and for team practice sessions.
- collect 3 to 5 strong clips for each stage
- add typical mistakes with a short breakdown, with rep names removed
- refresh the set every month from new calls
- have new hires listen to the set before their first solo calls
If your team sells in more than one language, build a separate library for each: a line that lands well in Russian does not always work in English. We train teams on the CRM and on call reports in our team training sessions .
## Software scores every call, the manager reviews the flagged ones
No manager can listen to every conversation, and a random sample misses patterns. So the split is simple: call speech analytics transcribes and scores every call against your criteria, shows average scores by rep and stage, and suggests who needs coaching. The manager spends time only on the calls the system has flagged. The agent works on the same CRM data as our other AI agents .
Pricing: 5,000 minutes for AED 1,000 a month, 10,000 minutes for AED 1,700, and from AED 4,000 for 30,000 minutes or more. When a sample is enough and when you need full coverage is covered in our guide on call quality control . If your calls mix languages, we test transcription quality on your own recordings before launch.
For any of this to work, recordings have to land in the CRM together with the client record. What to check with your telephony provider before connecting is in our news piece on telephony for a CRM in the UAE .
## A worked example: a team of 10 reps
A hypothetical Dubai company sells services over the phone and is sure it loses clients on price. Once every call is scored across the six blocks, the picture changes: most reps score low on the next step, and calls end without a date. For two months the sales manager coaches everyone on that stage only, and the script gets a mandatory question about the date of the next contact. After a month the manager checks whether that score has moved, and only then picks the next skill.
Follow-up after the call is picked up by the AI sales manager : it reminds a rep who has not messaged the client and replies when the rep goes quiet. All prices are on the pricing page .
## Questions and answers
**What criteria should I use to score sales calls?**
A solid baseline is opening, discovery, pitch, objection handling, next step, and delivery. For each criterion, write down what counts as done so that different reviewers give the same score.
**How many calls should I review with a rep?**
For a one-to-one, 2 or 3 calls showing the same mistake plus one good call is enough. Regularity matters more: a short weekly session on one skill.
**How much does call speech analytics cost?**
With MakeBiz Technologies, 5,000 minutes cost AED 1,000 a month, 10,000 minutes AED 1,700, and 30,000 minutes or more from AED 4,000. Prices exclude VAT.
**Can you analyse calls in English and Russian?**
We work in English and Russian, and we write the scoring criteria in your team's language. We test transcription quality on your own recordings before launch, especially where calls mix languages.
**Does the software replace the sales manager?**
No. It scores conversations and shows where the problem is, but rewriting the script and coaching the rep is still a person's job.

# Sales automation: from lead to payment
Deals are not lost on the big steps but in the gaps between them. Here is how to connect enquiries, the CRM, an AI agent and your accounting system so a deal reaches payment without anyone retyping data.
Lead-to-payment sales automation connects your web forms and WhatsApp, the CRM deal, the invoice in your accounting system and the payment status, with no manual data entry in between. With MakeBiz Technologies, Bitrix24 setup starts at AED 10,000 with go-live from 14 days, integration with Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo starts at AED 10,000, and an AI agent starts at AED 5,000.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## Sales automation closes the gaps between stages
Sales teams rarely lose money on one big step, they lose it in the gaps: a website enquiry sits unanswered for half an hour, a rep forgets to follow up after sending a quote, the invoice goes out two days after the client said yes, and nobody marks the payment in the CRM. Together these gaps stretch the deal and hand the client to whoever replied faster.
Automating the path from lead to payment removes those gaps. Data moves from stage to stage without anyone retyping it, and every step has an owner: a CRM automation rule, an AI agent or a sales rep. The sales manager can see where a deal is stuck before the client walks away.
## Every stage of the deal gets an owner
The key decision is which step goes to a rule, which to AI and which stays with a person. A typical split for B2B sales in the UAE:
| Stage | What happens | Who does it
| Enquiry | A web form, WhatsApp chat or call creates a lead with its source | CRM automation
| First reply | The client gets an answer while the rep is busy | AI agent
| Routing | The lead goes to a rep by product line, language or queue | CRM automation
| Qualification and quote | Understand the need, prepare the proposal | Sales rep, with the agent drafting
| Pipeline control | Reminders, stalled deals, alerts to the manager | AI agent
| Invoice | An AED invoice with 5% VAT is raised from the deal | Accounting system via integration
| Payment | Payment status flows back and the deal closes | Integration and CRM automation
MakeBiz Technologies blueprint for a typical project. The split changes to fit your process.
## CRM automation handles the rules
Anything that reads "if X, then Y" is a job for Bitrix24 automation rules: cheap, predictable, no AI needed.
- create a lead from a CRM form and keep the UTM tags
- route enquiries between reps by queue or product line
- set a call-back task if the client has not replied
- move the stage when a quote is sent or an invoice is issued
- alert the manager if a deal has not moved for longer than a set period
Automation rules are part of our standard Bitrix24 setup , which starts at AED 10,000 with go-live from 14 days. Connecting WhatsApp to open channels costs AED 500, with the provider subscription on top, see WhatsApp and messengers .
## An AI agent takes the steps that need language and judgement
A rule cannot give a client a proper answer or notice that a deal has stalled because the client is unsure about price. That calls for an agent. The AI sales manager replies to the client when the rep goes quiet and keeps an eye on the pipeline: it flags deals that have stopped moving and tells the manager where help is needed. The agent connects to your CRM and messengers, so it works with the same data as your team.
We explain the difference between an agent and an automation rule in our news piece AI agent or CRM automation . The short version: rules go to automation, conversations and judgement calls go to the agent, and decisions on discounts and terms stay with the rep. The Start package with one agent is AED 5,000 one-off, and maintenance is 10% of the implementation cost per month.

## Your accounting system issues the AED invoice with 5% VAT
The most common break sits between the CRM and finance: the rep agrees terms, messages the accountant, the invoice is created by hand, and the rep hears about payment from the client.
An integration fixes this. The Bitrix24 deal creates an invoice in Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo with the line items, the AED amount and 5% VAT. When accounting records the payment, the status flows back to the CRM and an automation rule closes the deal. Tax settings and company details are set by your finance team in the accounting system, and the integration simply uses them. Accounting integration with us starts at AED 10,000, see the scope on our Bitrix24 integrations page. For the UAE move to electronic invoicing, see our news on e-invoicing .
## Roll it out step by step
- Map the process as it is: where enquiries come from, who answers, where deals wait the longest
- Set up the pipeline and stages with clear exit criteria
- Connect the channels: website CRM forms, WhatsApp, telephony
- Add automation rules: routing, tasks, alerts
- Connect the CRM to accounting for invoices and payments
- Add the AI agent for first replies and pipeline control
- Train the team, and after a month check where deals still wait
To measure the effect, record three numbers from last month before go-live: time to first reply, time from the client saying yes to the invoice going out, and the share of deals with no activity for over a week. A month after launch compare them to see which step worked.
Order matters: an agent on a messy pipeline with no stages or rules will chase the wrong deals. For getting reps up to speed, see Bitrix24 training . To see which channel brings in paying deals, add end-to-end analytics .
## A worked example: a distributor with 15 sales reps
A hypothetical equipment distributor in Dubai gets enquiries from its website and on WhatsApp. Reps answer from their personal phones, the accountant raises invoices in QuickBooks after a chat message, and the sales team learns about payments late.
After automation, every enquiry becomes a lead with a source, the AI sales manager replies on WhatsApp when the rep is busy, the invoice is created from the deal, and the payment closes the deal on its own. One-off costs: Bitrix24 setup from AED 10,000, WhatsApp AED 500, QuickBooks integration from AED 10,000 and an AI agent from AED 5,000. ## Questions and answers
**Where should sales automation start?**
With a map of the process as it is: where enquiries come from, who answers and where deals wait the longest. Then you set up the pipeline, channels and automation rules, and only after that add an AI agent.
**What is the difference between CRM automation and an AI agent?**
An automation rule runs "if X, then Y": create a lead, set a task, move a stage. An agent understands text and context: it replies to clients, spots stalled deals and tells the manager about them.
**Can I issue invoices with 5% VAT straight from Bitrix24?**
The invoice is triggered from the deal, but your accounting system produces it: Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo. Your finance team sets up tax, and the integration passes deal data across and returns the payment status.

Title: RPA vs AI agents: which to choose for automation | MakeBiz

Journal · Automation
# RPA or AI agents: which to choose for automation
RPA and AI agents are often pitched as two versions of the same thing. They are not. They solve different problems, and the right choice depends on what kind of data flows through your process.
If a task follows fixed rules and the data always sits in the same fields, RPA or CRM automation rules will do the job. If the process involves emails, chats, PDFs and exceptions, you need an AI agent: at MakeBiz Technologies one agent costs from AED 5,000 one-off, a team of agents from AED 10,000, and ongoing support is 10% of the implementation cost per month. Often it pays to combine them: rules and integrations take the predictable part, the agent takes whatever the rules cannot cover.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## RPA repeats actions, an AI agent works with meaning
RPA (robotic process automation) is a software bot that mimics what a person does on screen: it opens a system, copies a value from one window to another and clicks buttons according to a script. It does not understand the work, but repeats it the same way a thousand times.
An AI agent works differently. It reads an email, a client's WhatsApp message or a supplier quote, understands what it is about and decides the next step: reply, create a task, compare prices or hand over to a person. We covered how an agent differs from a standard CRM automation rule in our news piece on AI agents vs CRM automation .
The rule of thumb: RPA automates actions, an agent automates decisions. If there is nothing to decide in a process, you do not need an agent.
## The type of task decides the tool
Break the process down by type of work, not by department. This is the comparison we bring to a first client meeting.
| Task | RPA or CRM rule | AI agent
| Moving data between systems with identical fields | Works if the system has no API | Overkill
| Creating a deal from a website form | A CRM rule handles it | Not needed
| Sorting incoming emails and messages | Cannot read free text | Fits: understands the request and replies
| Comparing supplier quotes in PDF | Breaks on different layouts | Fits: builds a comparison table
| Replying when a sales rep goes quiet | Only a timed template | Answers the actual question
| Matching payments by exact references | Works | Only for exceptions
| Scoring sales calls | Not applicable | Fits: scores every call
MakeBiz Technologies comparison of typical tasks, November 2026. We test your own process in a demo.
## RPA wins where the rules never change
A bot is a good fit when a task ticks three boxes: the input always comes in the same format, the steps are known in advance, and a mistake shows up immediately. Say, pulling a bank statement into a spreadsheet, moving orders out of a legacy system with no API, or checking order statuses on a supplier portal every morning.
The weak spot of RPA: it depends on the user interface. A button moves, a field is added, the supplier site gets slower, and the script stops. So when a system has an API, we suggest a proper integration first rather than a bot clicking over the screen. For linking a CRM with accounting in the UAE that usually means Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo, and we build that integration with Bitrix24 from AED 10,000.
Much of what companies call RPA is really covered by standard Bitrix24 automation rules: tasks, stage changes, templates, payment reminders. That is cheaper to run than a separate RPA platform.

We will show what a CRM rule can handle and what needs an agent. One agent from AED 5,000 one-off, a 30 to 40 minute demo is free
Book a demo
## An AI agent belongs where there is text, exceptions and conversation
The signs of an agent task are the opposite: the input is different every time, the rules are described with words like "usually" and "it depends", and today the work is done by someone who reads and thinks. Typical places:
- inbound leads on WhatsApp and email, where clients write however they like. The AI sales manager covers this: it replies when a rep goes quiet and watches the pipeline
- procurement: sending requests to suppliers and comparing quotes that arrive in all sorts of formats. That is the Procurement agent
- finance: a summary of cash and variances for the business owner
- hiring: the first screening interview with a candidate
An agent has its own kind of error. It can misread an unusual case, so anything involving money or a promise to a client is designed with human approval until the agent has built up a track record on your data.
## A bot, an integration and an agent together cover the whole process
Real processes are rarely either-or. A lead comes in, a CRM rule creates a deal, the agent reads the message and works out what the client needs, the accounting integration issues an invoice in AED with 5% VAT, and a person steps in to approve a discount.
How to map a process into these points is covered in our guide on where an AI agent fits into a business process , and the Bitrix24 with AI page explains how the CRM and agents work together.

With RPA the main costs are the platform licence at the vendor's rates and script fixes every time an interface changes. With an agent it is the implementation plus monthly support.
- Work out how many hours a month the task takes today and who does it
- Estimate what share of cases follows the rules and what share needs a judgement call
- Price a CRM rule or an integration for the rule-based share, and an agent for the rest
- Add support: 10% of the implementation cost per month for an agent, script maintenance for RPA

A bot on the inbox will not help, since every email is different. RPA repeats predefined on-screen actions from a script and does not understand the content. An AI agent reads text, understands what it means and picks the next step, so it copes with emails, chats and mixed-format documents.
**Can Bitrix24 automation replace RPA?**

# Procurement automation: from purchase request to supplier choice
In a small or mid-sized company, purchasing usually lives in email, WhatsApp and Excel: requests arrive in a group chat, RFQs go out by hand and quotes end up in a spreadsheet nobody can find later. Here is which stages a system can take over and what stays with your buyer.
Procurement automation covers the path from purchase request to supplier choice: a request in the CRM, RFQs sent from a specification, quotes collected, compared on price, lead time and terms, then approved. The MakeBiz Technologies procurement AI agent handles the RFQs, follow-ups and quote consolidation, while the decision stays with a person. MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 8 min read
## Purchasing runs in six stages, and each has an owner
Before you automate anything, break the process into stages. Most companies have six, even if nobody calls them that. The table shows who runs each stage once it is automated and where the data ends up.
| Stage | What happens | Who does it after automation | Where the data lives
| 1. Request | Someone states what they need, how many and by when | The employee fills in a CRM form | Request record
| 2. Approval | A manager confirms the need and the budget | A CRM automation rule routes it by amount | Request record
| 3. RFQs | The specification goes to several suppliers | The AI agent sends RFQs and chases replies | Emails and chats in the CRM
| 4. Quote collection | Replies arrive as PDFs, Excel files, emails and WhatsApp messages | The AI agent reads them and maps them to line items | Documents in the record
| 5. Comparison and choice | Prices, lead times and terms are put side by side | The agent builds the table, the buyer decides | Comparison table in the CRM
| 6. Order and delivery | Purchase order, payment, delivery tracking | CRM rules create tasks, the buyer manages it | Deal and accounting system
MakeBiz Technologies outline for routine purchases of goods and services, excluding formal tenders.
Stages three to five carry most of the manual work, so that is where the agent goes. The rest is ordinary CRM automation.
## Requests belong in the CRM, not in a group chat
Automation starts with a request form, not with AI. A voice note in a group chat tells no system what to buy. In Bitrix24 a purchase request works well as a separate smart process with its own stages: new, awaiting approval, RFQ sent, comparison, ordered, closed. See how these are built on our Bitrix24 development page.
Required fields:
- item or catalogue reference, quantity and unit of measure
- required date and delivery address: warehouse, office or site
- budget estimate and the cost centre it is charged to
- attachments: photo, drawing or specification, if there is one
Without these fields a request does not move on. A CRM rule sends it to the line manager, and above a threshold you set, to the finance director too. No AI needed here.
## The agent takes over RFQs and supplier follow-ups
After approval comes the part buyers like least: sending the specification, chasing silent suppliers and tracking who got what. The procurement agent does this itself: it takes suppliers for the category from your database, sends the RFQ by email or messenger and follows up with anyone who has not replied.
Every message is saved in the request record, so history stays when people leave. If your suppliers work on WhatsApp, the channel is connected to the CRM through the official platform, see our messengers in Bitrix24 page. The agent does not promise volumes and does not negotiate: if a supplier asks something outside the specification, the question goes to the buyer.

## Quotes go into one table on one basis
Replies come as scanned PDFs, long Excel price lists or a price typed into an email. The agent reads each document and maps it to the request line items: unit price, currency, VAT included or on top, lead time, stock, payment terms, warranty. What this kind of extraction can do and where it stops is covered in our guide to invoice and document recognition .
What matters in a comparison is not speed but a common basis. Prices are converted to one currency at a recorded rate and date, all amounts are shown excluding VAT, and the tax (the standard UAE rate is 5%) sits in its own column. The four places where money leaks during consolidation are covered in our news piece on comparing suppliers , and a table template with every column is in the guide to comparing supplier quotes .
Lines that do not add up are flagged, so the buyer reviews those instead of the whole table.
## The decision and the accountability stay with a person
The agent prepares the choice, it does not make it. Some criteria are written down nowhere: the supplier who saved you on an urgent order, a cheap newcomer with no track record, a discount agreed in a meeting. The buyer sees the table and the agent's reasoning, then decides.
These stay with people:
- negotiating price and terms, especially with key suppliers
- choosing a new supplier for an important category
- exceptions: urgent orders, a single source, unusual payment terms
- signing the purchase order or contract
The line between an AI agent and a CRM automation rule is explained on our AI in Bitrix24 page. In short: a rule executes a condition, an agent works with text and documents, and a person owns the decision.

Page: https://makebiztechnologies.com/en/journal/invoice-document-recognition
Title: AI invoice and document recognition: what it does | MakeBiz

Journal · Documents
# AI invoice and document recognition: what it does and where it stops
Invoices, quotes, price lists and delivery notes reach you by email and WhatsApp in every possible format, and someone still types them into the CRM and the accounts. Here is what AI can pull out of documents, where it gets things wrong and how to test it on your own files.
AI document recognition extracts the supplier, number, date, amounts, VAT and line items from invoices, quotes and price lists, checks them against the purchase order and passes only the doubtful cases to a person. It stops at poor scans, handwritten notes and payment decisions, which an employee reviews. MakeBiz Technologies builds recognition into its procurement and finance agents: one agent is AED 5,000 one-off, and we show how it handles your own documents in a free demo.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## OCR reads characters, Document AI understands the document
OCR (optical character recognition) turns an image into text: letters and digits, with no meaning attached. It does not know which number is the invoice total and which is a phone number, and it needs a template for every document layout. Document AI goes further: it finds fields by meaning, rebuilds the line item table and knows that "Total incl. VAT" on one invoice and "Grand total" on another are the same field.
| Task | OCR | Document AI | Person
| Text from a scan or photo | Yes, that is its core job | Uses OCR as the first step | Not needed
| Supplier, number, date, total | Only with a template per layout | By meaning, no template per supplier | Reviews doubtful cases
| Line items: quantity, price, amount | Tables often break apart | Yes, quality depends on the source | Reviews flagged lines
| Match to PO and price list | No | Yes, if the CRM and accounts are connected | Resolves mismatches
| Approve payment | No | No | Yes
MakeBiz Technologies comparison for typical incoming document tasks.
## Results depend on the source file
The same engine gives different results on different files. This is what usually lands in a company's inbox:
- a PDF exported from the supplier's accounting system: the text is already inside the file, which makes it the most reliable case
- a scan: much depends on resolution and on stamps or signatures over the figures
- a phone photo: skew, shadows, cropped edges
- a table in an email body or a WhatsApp message: the text is there, but the structure is loose
- an Excel price list: exact figures, but every supplier uses different columns
That is why an accuracy figure "in general" tells you very little. Until extraction has been tested on your own document flow, any number is just a number on a slide.
## Invoice headers are easier than line items
Header fields appear on almost every invoice: supplier and tax registration number (TRN), document number and date, currency, total and VAT amount. Document AI handles these with confidence. Line items are harder: a table running over several pages, a description wrapped onto two lines, the same product in different pack sizes, a discount on its own line at the bottom.
Simple arithmetic helps here, and the system runs it on its own:
- quantity times unit price equals the line amount
- the sum of the lines equals the total before tax
- the VAT amount matches the base at the rate stated on the document (the standard UAE rate is 5%)
If any check fails, the document is flagged and goes to a person. This is not a tax review, it is a check that the numbers were read correctly.
## We test English and Arabic on your own documents
In the UAE documents arrive in English, sometimes in Arabic or in both at once, and overseas suppliers add their own formats. We do not promise the same quality for every language and layout up front. Arabic text, bilingual invoices and handwritten notes are tested on your real files before launch, and only then do we agree which fields are captured automatically and which stay with manual review. We work in English and Russian, and an Arabic interface is not part of the offer.
### See extraction on your own documents
Invoices, quotes and price lists into your CRM and accounts without retyping, doubtful cases set aside. One agent AED 5,000 one-off
Book a demo
## The line sits where a mistake costs money
High accuracy on a single field and reliability of the whole process are two different things, as we explain in our news piece on why invoices still contain errors at 98% accuracy . The practical takeaway is simple: the system has to know when it is unsure and stop, rather than write a guess into your books.
Rules we set up in almost every project:
- PO matching: items and prices on the invoice are checked against the order, and any mismatch goes to a person
- duplicates: same supplier, number and amount get flagged before payment
- a new supplier or changed bank details: always reviewed by hand
- amounts above a threshold you set: confirmed by an employee
- payments: the AI never sends them
The result is that people work on exceptions, not on the whole document flow.
## Recognition belongs inside a process, not in a standalone tool
Extracted data is only useful if it lands where people use it. In purchasing, supplier quotes go straight into a comparison table: that is how the procurement agent works, and the table template is in our guide to comparing supplier quotes . In finance, the finance agent collects invoices and bank statements and shows cash by business line.
The original document is stored in the CRM record next to the extracted data, so any value can be checked against the source. If the data has to reach Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo, you need an accounting system integration , which starts from AED 10,000. Where recognition fits on the path from request to order is covered in our guide to procurement automation .
## Testing starts with your own documents
- Collect real documents from a normal month: clean PDFs, poor scans, photos, bilingual invoices
- Demo: 30 to 40 minutes, free, we show extraction on your own process
- Agree which fields you need and which system they go to
- Set the matching rules and the thresholds for manual review
- Launch one flow, such as supplier invoices, then extend
One agent on the Start package is AED 5,000 one-off, procurement and finance together on the Business package are AED 10,000, and support is 10% of the implementation fee per month. All prices are on our pricing page .
A hypothetical example: a distributor receives supplier invoices by email, some as PDFs, some as stamped scans. After launch the agent reads each invoice, matches it to the order in the CRM and lets through only those where everything agrees. The accountant opens a queue of flagged documents instead of the whole flow.
## Questions and answers
**How is OCR different from AI document recognition?**
OCR turns an image into text but does not know where the total or the invoice number is. Document AI finds fields by meaning, rebuilds line items and checks the figures against each other.
**Can AI read scans and photos?**
Yes, but quality depends on the source: low resolution, stamps over figures, skew and shadows all reduce reliability. Those documents are more likely to be flagged for manual review.
**Does recognition work with Arabic?**
We test it on your documents before launch. Arabic text, bilingual invoices and handwritten notes behave differently depending on the file, so we do not quote accuracy percentages in advance.
**Can we take people out of invoice entry completely?**
You should not. The system takes the routine off the main flow, and an employee reviews PO mismatches, duplicates, new suppliers and large amounts.
**How much does document recognition cost?**
Recognition runs inside the procurement and finance agents: one agent is AED 5,000 one-off, two on the Business package are AED 10,000. Support is 10% of the implementation fee per month.
