Journal · Analytics
# End-to-end marketing analytics: from ad click to payment
Your ad account counts clicks, your CRM counts deals and your finance team counts money. End-to-end analytics brings them together and shows which channel really brings in payments.
End-to-end analytics links every payment to the ad that produced it: UTM tags and click IDs are saved in the CRM deal, and the payment comes in from your accounting system. With MakeBiz Technologies, Bitrix24 CRM setup starts at AED 10,000, integration with Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo starts at AED 10,000, and the end-to-end dashboard in MakeBiz BI is part of the Pro plan at AED 1,000 a month, with the first 14 days free.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## End-to-end analytics answers one question: which channel brings in money
Your ad account sees clicks and leads. Your CRM sees deals. Your accounting system sees payments. Each is accurate on its own, yet none can say how much revenue your Google Ads budget returned. End-to-end analytics joins them into one chain, so every payment has a source.
Without it, budgets are set on cost per lead. A channel with cheap leads looks like a winner even if those leads never pay, and a channel with expensive leads gets paused although it brings the large deals. End-to-end analytics swaps that for cost per paying customer and return on ad spend by source.
## The chain has five links
Data travels from click to money through five systems, and a break in any of them cuts the chain.
| Link | What is passed on | Where it lives | What usually breaks
| Ads | Spend, clicks, campaign | Google Ads, Meta Ads | Campaigns named differently in each account
| Website and form | UTM tags, gclid, fbclid | Hidden form fields | Tags are lost as the visitor moves between pages
| WhatsApp and calls | Lead source | Open channels, telephony | A WhatsApp chat or a call arrives with no tag
| CRM | Lead, deal, amount, stage | Bitrix24 | Duplicate contacts, deals created by hand with no source
| Accounting | Invoice and payment | Zoho Books, QuickBooks, Odoo | The invoice is not linked to the deal
MakeBiz Technologies blueprint for a typical project. The links you need depend on your channels.
## Tracking rules come before the first campaign
The most common reason for gaps in the report: ads went live before anyone agreed on tagging. A month later the CRM is full of deals with the source "website" and no campaign behind them.
- One UTM convention. utm_source for the platform, utm_medium for the traffic type, utm_campaign for the campaign. Names in lowercase Latin letters, spelled the same way in every ad account
- Click IDs. Google Ads auto-tagging adds gclid, Meta adds fbclid. Store them in the deal so you can send the payment back to the ad platform later
- Hidden form fields. A Bitrix24 CRM form reads the tags from the page URL and writes them into the lead, so sales reps type nothing
- Dedicated entry points. A WhatsApp link or number per campaign, and a separate phone number per source for calls
In the UAE many customers message on WhatsApp or call instead of filling in a form, and that is where tags go missing. Our news piece on the AI agent in WhatsApp covers the channel side, and our piece on telephony for your CRM lists what to check with your carrier. We connect WhatsApp to Bitrix24 for AED 500 plus the provider subscription, see WhatsApp and messengers in Bitrix24 .
### We build the chain from click to payment
UTM tags in CRM forms, a source on every deal, payments from accounting and a dashboard by channel on the BI Pro plan, AED 1,000 a month
Talk about analytics
## Revenue comes from accounting, not from the deal stage
A deal marked "Won" means the rep closed it, not that the money is in the bank: the client may pay in part, late or not at all. So the last link comes from accounting. The invoice is raised from the deal, and the payment status flows back to the CRM on its own.
We integrate Bitrix24 with Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo from AED 10,000, the scope is on our integrations page . Agree which figure counts as revenue: UAE invoices include 5% VAT, so label amounts as gross or net of VAT.
## Setting it up is a step-by-step job
- List every source: ad accounts, website, WhatsApp, phone, partners, repeat business
- Sign off the UTM convention and campaign naming, and share it with everyone who launches ads
- Configure CRM forms and open channels so tags land in the lead without the rep touching them
- Make the source field mandatory, with a fixed list of values for deals created by hand
- Connect the CRM to accounting so payments flow back into the deal
- Pull spend from the ad platforms into BI and match it with payments by campaign
- After 2 to 4 weeks, reconcile the report with the ad accounts and finance
Check the quality of older deals first: duplicates and empty fields damage a report more than missing tags, see our guide on why CRM reports lie . You can also order a stand-alone Bitrix24 audit .
## The dashboard shows cost per payment, not cost per lead
The result is one table by source and a few charts. Core metrics:
- spend per channel and number of leads
- deals and payments from those leads
- cost per lead and cost per paying customer
- revenue and return on ad spend by channel
- average time from lead to payment
The last one matters for long B2B deals: if clients pay two months after the first enquiry, last month's campaigns have not shown results yet. End-to-end analytics by CRM UTM data, with ad spend added, is part of the Pro plan of MakeBiz BI analytics at AED 1,000 a month, while ad accounts and accounting systems are connected to BI on request for an extra fee. The first 14 days are free, and the trial runs on the full Pro plan. Which other views a sales director needs is covered in our news on three sales dashboards .
It also pays to send payments back to the ad platforms. Google Ads supports offline conversion imports by gclid, and Meta offers the Conversions API. The platforms then optimise for paying customers, not for everyone who left a number.
## A worked example: a trading company with 10 sales reps
A hypothetical Dubai trading company runs Google Ads and Meta, and leads arrive by web form, WhatsApp and phone. Half the CRM deals have no source, and finance tracks payments in Zoho Books. The owner sees that Meta delivers cheap leads and wants to move the whole budget there.

## Questions and answers
**What is end-to-end analytics in plain terms?**
It is a report in which every payment has an ad source. Data from the ad accounts, the CRM and accounting is linked, so you can see how much money each channel brought in.
**Can I do end-to-end analytics without a CRM?**
Only partly, because without a CRM you cannot see which leads became deals and payments. The minimum is an ad account, a CRM with a source on every deal and payments from accounting.

Page: https://makebiztechnologies.com/en/journal/call-quality-team-vs-system
Title: Call quality control: QA team, software or both | MakeBiz

Journal · AI agents
# Call quality control: QA team, software or both
Sooner or later every company with a sales team has to decide who listens to the calls: a QA specialist, call speech analytics software, or both. The answer depends on your call volume and on what you actually want to find out.
A QA specialist listens to a sample and is good at unpacking individual calls, software scores 100% of calls and spots patterns, and in practice the combination works: the software scores every call, a person reviews the flagged ones and coaches the reps. MakeBiz call speech analytics costs AED 1,000 a month for 5,000 minutes, AED 1,700 for 10,000 minutes and from AED 4,000 for 30,000 minutes or more.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## Sampling and full coverage answer different questions
Sampling answers the question "how did this rep handle these calls". Full coverage answers "what is happening across every call the team makes". They are different jobs, and mixing them up leads to the wrong conclusions.
Say calls break down at the same stage in a noticeable share of conversations. If a QA specialist listens to a handful of calls per rep each week, they may spot the pattern or they may not: it all depends on which calls landed in the sample. Software that looks at every call shows the share of those calls for each rep. We walked through one such breaking point in our news piece on where sales teams lose clients inside the call .
## The three approaches differ in coverage and the human role
| Criterion | QA team | Call speech analytics | Both
| Coverage | A sample of calls | 100% of calls | Software covers all, a person reviews the flagged ones
| What it finds | Mistakes in specific calls, nuances of tone | Patterns by stage, rep and objection | Both
| Speed | Depends on the specialist's hours | Once the recording is processed | System report, reviews on a schedule
| Consistency | Depends on the reviewer | The same criteria for every call | Shared criteria, a person settles disputes
| Coaching reps | A real strength | Suggestions, not mentoring | Coaching based on flagged calls
| Main costs | Salary and the specialist's time | Subscription by minutes | Subscription plus part of a specialist's time
MakeBiz Technologies comparison, November 2026. Software prices are on our pricing page, staff costs vary by company.
## Do the maths in call minutes
To compare the options, work out your call volume in minutes: number of reps, times calls per day, times average call length, times working days. Take a hypothetical team: 6 reps, 20 calls a day each, 3 minutes on average, 22 working days. That is 2,640 calls and 7,920 minutes a month, or 132 hours of recordings.
No one person can listen to 132 hours a month and still do anything else, and scoring takes time on top of listening. That is why a QA team always works with a sample. For example, 5 calls per rep per week gives you 120 calls a month out of 2,640, about 4.5% of conversations and roughly 6 hours of pure listening.
For software, that volume fits the 10,000-minute plan at AED 1,700 a month. Under 5,000 minutes the AED 1,000 plan is enough, and larger teams with 30,000 minutes or more start from AED 4,000. All plans are on the pricing page .
To keep the comparison fair, the cost of a QA specialist is more than a salary: add the manager's time spent checking their scores, and onboarding a replacement if they leave. Software costs are more predictable, because the subscription depends on minutes, not people.
### We score 100% of your team's calls
Scores by stage and rep, top objections. 5,000 minutes AED 1,000 a month, 10,000 minutes AED 1,700
Price it for my team
## You still need a QA person with software in place
Software does not replace someone who understands your product and your clients. It will not judge whether a rep picked the right moment for a discount on an unusual deal, and it will not have the conversation with a rep who is burning out. A person is needed for three things:
- setting and refining the criteria: what a good call means in your business
- reviewing disputed and high-stakes calls: a large deal, a complaint, a lost client
- mentoring: the one-to-one, practice, and a check a week later
How to run those reviews is covered in our guide on sales call analysis . We train managers and QA staff to work with the reports in our team training sessions .
## Software takes the routine and surfaces patterns
Call speech analytics transcribes every conversation, scores it against the stages of your script, collects the top client questions and objections, tracks each rep over time and suggests who needs coaching. The call summary and score appear in the deal record, next to the chat history.
The big change is that nobody spends time hunting for problem calls any more. The QA person opens the report, sees where scores drop and listens to exactly those calls. If you only have two reps and a light call load, software may be overkill and a sample will do.
Full coverage has another benefit: scores are comparable across reps and months. When every call is judged by the same criteria, the "I was marked harder than my colleague" argument goes away, and coaching is about numbers rather than impressions.
## The combined setup runs on a simple cycle
- Agree the scoring criteria with the head of sales and write them up for your script
- The software scores every call and updates the report
- Once a week the QA specialist takes the flagged calls and reviews them
- The sales manager runs short one-to-ones with reps, one skill at a time
- Once a month the criteria are checked against reality and the wording is refined
Calls are only part of the client conversation. WhatsApp follow-up and pipeline control are handled by the AI sales manager , and call recordings need to land in the CRM: what to check with your telephony provider is in our news piece on telephony for a CRM in the UAE .
## A worked example: a team of 6 reps
A hypothetical Abu Dhabi company has one QA specialist who listens to about 5 calls per rep each week. Once the software is connected, they stop searching for problem calls by hand and spend the same hours reviewing flagged calls and coaching. The sales manager sees every rep's score by stage, not just the reviewer's impressions. After a quarter the company decides whether it needs a second QA person based on data, not on how busy everyone feels.
Software cost for around 7,920 minutes a month: AED 1,700 on the 10,000-minute plan, excluding VAT. A demo on your process is free and takes 30 to 40 minutes. The other agents that work on the same CRM data are on the AI agents page.
## Questions and answers
**Should I hire a QA specialist or use call speech analytics?**
It depends on call volume. With a light call load, a sample reviewed by a person is enough. With hundreds of calls a day, software scores all of them and a person reviews the flagged ones and coaches reps.
**How much does call speech analytics cost?**
5,000 minutes cost AED 1,000 a month, 10,000 minutes AED 1,700, and 30,000 minutes or more from AED 4,000. Prices exclude VAT.
**How do I estimate my monthly call minutes?**
Multiply the number of reps by calls per day, average call length and working days. For a more accurate figure, export last month's data from your telephony or CRM.
**Can I drop manual call listening completely?**
We would not recommend it. Software finds the problem calls, but the criteria, disputed cases and coaching stay with a person.
**Can reps see their own scores?**
The score and call summary appear in the deal record. Who sees which reports is set by CRM permissions: usually a rep sees their own calls and the manager sees the whole team.

Title: Bitrix24 smart processes: what and when to use | MakeBiz

Journal · Bitrix24
# Bitrix24 smart processes: what they are and when you need them
Once your sales pipeline fills with cards that are not sales, the portal starts confusing everyone. Bitrix24 smart processes give those processes a place of their own. Here is how they work and when they are worth it.
A Bitrix24 smart process is a custom CRM entity with its own stages, fields, permissions and automation rules, built for purchase requests, contracts, service requests and anything else that does not fit into a deal. You need one when a process has its own path, its own people and needs its own report. MakeBiz Technologies sets up smart processes as part of an implementation with the standard setup from AED 10,000, or separately at AED 200 an hour, with the quote fixed before work starts.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## A smart process is a CRM entity of its own, next to deals
Bitrix24 CRM comes with standard entities: leads, deals, contacts, companies, quotes and invoices. They describe a sale well. But a company runs other processes too: a department's purchase request, a contract going through sign-off, a client's service request after the sale. Put those into deals and the sales pipeline fills with cards that are not sales, while revenue reports stop adding up.
A smart process fixes that. An administrator creates a new entity with its own name, and it gets everything a deal has:
- its own kanban stages and, if needed, several pipelines
- its own fields: amounts, dates, lists, files, links to employees
- links to contacts, companies, deals and other smart processes
- automation rules and triggers on stages, just like the sales pipeline
- separate access rights: who can see, create and move items
- documents generated from templates right inside the item
Whether smart processes are available, and how many, depends on the Bitrix24 plan, so we check the plan before quoting.
## Deals, smart processes, tasks and workflows do different jobs
The usual problem in a portal is not a lack of tools but mixing them up. This table helps decide where a process belongs.
| Tool | What it is for | Tell-tale sign
| Deal | A sale to a client | There is an amount, a probability and sales stages
| Smart process | A recurring process with its own stages: purchasing, contracts, service | Many similar items, each with its own path and people
| Task | A one-off assignment | One person, one result, no stages
| Workflow (business process) | A chain of steps with conditions and approvals | Branching logic on top of any entity
Smart processes and workflows are not rivals. Stages and items live in the smart process, and a branching approval runs as a workflow at the right stage. Simple actions such as creating a task, changing the owner or sending a notification are handled by automation rules.
## Purchase requests travel from request to payment in one item
Take a hypothetical trading company: departments send purchase requests in a group chat, the finance director approves them in private messages, and a month later nobody remembers who signed off what. A "Purchase request" smart process puts it all in one item.
- New. An employee fills in what is needed, how many and by when
- Approval. A rule sends an approval task to the line manager, and anything above a threshold goes to the finance director
- Quotes. The buyer requests supplier quotes and attaches them to the item
- Ordered. A supplier is chosen and the item is linked to its company record
- Received and closed. Delivery is confirmed, then payment
Collecting and comparing quotes can go to the procurement AI agent : it sends requests to suppliers and puts the quotes side by side. Where money leaks at this step is covered in our news on comparing suppliers .
### We build smart processes around how you work
Purchasing, contracts, service: stages, permissions, rules and document templates at AED 200 an hour, quote fixed upfront
Discuss your process
## Contracts get their own stages and deadlines
A contract is linked to a deal and a company, but it outlives the sale. In a "Contracts" smart process it has stages of its own: draft, review, client sign-off, signed, active, expiring. Fields hold the number, the amount in AED, the start date and the end date.
Automation rules do the rest: a set number of days before the end date the owner gets a task to talk to the client about renewal, and the document itself is generated from a template using the item's data. A rep opens the deal and sees the linked contract in a tab, with no digging through folders or email.
## Service requests show what happens after the sale
After a sale the client needs installation, maintenance or an answer to a complaint. If that runs through chats, the manager cannot see how many requests are open or how many are stuck. A "Service request" smart process is linked to the company and the deal, and a rep creates one from the client record in a click.
The stages are simple: received, assigned, in progress, waiting for client, done. A delayed rule reminds the engineer if a request sits too long on one stage, and the manager sees a kanban of every open request. If requests arrive on WhatsApp, the channel connects to Bitrix24 open channels, see the WhatsApp in Bitrix24 page.
## A smart process pays off when three signs are present
Not every process deserves its own entity. A smart process makes sense when:
- the process has its own stages, and dozens of similar items go through them
- different people or departments take part, and it matters who is on which step
- you need a report on it: how many items, at which stage, how long in progress
If it is really one or two fields on a deal ("delivery needed: yes or no"), a separate entity only makes the portal harder to use. If your portal has already collected spare pipelines and entities, start with a Bitrix24 audit . How a CRM automation rule differs from an AI agent in such processes is explained in our news on agents and CRM rules .
## What setup costs: a worked example
A hypothetical company with 30 staff wants three smart processes: purchasing, contracts and service. If fields, stages, permissions, rules and document templates take, say, 24 hours, that is AED 4,800 at AED 200 an hour. In a Bitrix24 implementation with the standard setup from AED 10,000, smart processes go into the overall quote, which is fixed before work starts. Linking a smart process to an external system or accounting is priced as development , and changes after go-live are easiest to run through support , for example a 10-hour package at AED 2,300 a month. All prices are on the pricing page .
## Questions and answers
**How is a smart process different from a deal?**
A deal describes a sale with an amount and stages. A smart process is a separate entity for another process, such as purchasing or contracts, with its own stages, fields and permissions, and it keeps the sales pipeline clean.
**Can a smart process be linked to deals and companies?**
Yes. A smart process links to contacts, companies, deals and other smart processes, and linked items show up in each other's tabs.
**Do automation rules and workflows work in smart processes?**
Yes. Automation rules and triggers are set on smart process stages, and workflows handle approvals with branching logic.
**Are smart processes available on every Bitrix24 plan?**
Availability and the number of smart processes depend on the plan. We check it before quoting so the process does not hit a limit after go-live.
**How much does it cost to set up a smart process?**
Work is billed at AED 200 an hour, with the scope fixed in the quote before work starts. In an implementation with the standard setup from AED 10,000, smart processes go into the overall quote.

# Bitrix24 implementation contract: what to include
CRM projects usually go wrong not because of bad setup but because the contract describes the scope in one line. Here are the clauses worth checking before you sign.
A Bitrix24 implementation contract should cover eight things: the list of work, what is excluded, stage deadlines (a standard launch with us takes from 14 days), acceptance, who owns the portal and access, how scope changes are handled, support and payment. MakeBiz Technologies contracts through MakeBiz Technologies FZE LLC, invoices in AED, fixes the quote before work starts and offers post-launch support from AED 1,250 for 5 hours a month.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## Scope is written as a list, not as the word "implementation"
A line that says "Bitrix24 CRM implementation" in the contract fixes nothing. A month in, the client assumes the accounting integration was included and the partner assumes it was not. So write the scope as a list of tasks with outcomes: a sales pipeline with these stages, roles and permissions for these groups, a WhatsApp channel connected, an invoice template with 5% VAT created.
The second list matters just as much: what the contract does not cover. Typically that is the Bitrix24 licence, paid third-party services, data migration, complex integrations and custom development. If an item appears in neither list, you will almost certainly argue about it later. Our standard setup is broken down in the guide to turnkey Bitrix24 implementation , and it works well as a starting point for your list.
This is a buyer's checklist, not legal advice: have your lawyer review the contract wording.
## Eight clauses prevent most disputes
| Clause | What to write down | What happens if you skip it
| Scope | A list of tasks, each with an outcome | Arguments over what the price covered
| Exclusions | Licence, services, migration, development | Surprise invoices halfway through
| Timeline | Stage dates and what the client provides for each | Delays nobody can explain
| Acceptance | Test scenarios and a deadline for feedback | A project that never closes
| Access and data | Who owns the portal, how access is granted and revoked | A portal that depends on the partner
| Change requests | How new work is estimated and at what rate | Extra work with no estimate or sign-off
| Support | Hours package, response time, how requests are logged | Nobody to fix things after go-live
| Payment | Currency, company details, schedule, taxes | Late payments and exchange rate surprises
The table does not replace a contract, but it is a quick pass before you sign. If the draft says nothing on two or three of these rows, ask the partner about them. We published a similar checklist for AI projects in our news on questions to ask a contractor before signing .
## Deadlines are tied to stages and to client decisions
A standard Bitrix24 launch with us takes from 14 days. In the contract, though, a single end date is less useful than stage dates: discovery, setup, training, handover. Next to each stage, note what the company has to provide: an owner on your side, the list of users, signed-off pipeline stages, a sample invoice, access to the portal.
That way both sides can see why a date moved. If signing off the stages took a week, setup starts a week later, and that is not the partner's breach. What makes UAE projects longer (multiple entities, accounting, migration, channels) is covered in our news on CRM implementation timelines .
### Get our draft contract before the call
List of work, stages, acceptance and a quote in AED. Standard setup from AED 10,000, launch from 14 days
Request the contract
## Acceptance runs on scenarios, not on impressions
"The system is set up" cannot be tested. Scenarios agreed in advance can. For example:
- a new WhatsApp message creates a lead and reaches the right rep
- a deal moves through every pipeline stage, and required fields stop anyone skipping a step
- an invoice in AED with 5% VAT goes out from the deal using your template
- a rep sees only their own deals, the manager sees the whole team
- automation rules create tasks and send notifications at the right stages
Add a feedback window, for example a few business days after handover, and one rule: a defect is something that does not work according to an agreed scenario. A new wish ("could we also get a report by emirate?") is a change request and is estimated separately. That split is what stops acceptance from dragging on forever.
## The portal, access and data stay with your company
The Bitrix24 portal and licence should be registered to your company, and the portal administrator should be one of your employees. The partner works under a separate user account that you can switch off at any time. Put it in writing:
- the portal, service accounts and data belong to the client
- the partner gets access for the duration of the work, and it is revoked at the end
- settings, templates and integration notes are handed over with the system
At MakeBiz Technologies this is a standard term: access and data stay with the client. How licences are issued and what plans exist is on the Bitrix24 licences page.
## Change requests and support get their own terms
Every project produces tasks that were not in the quote. A good contract says how to handle them: the partner gives an estimate in hours before starting, the client confirms in writing, and the work is billed at the agreed rate. With us, work beyond the standard scope is AED 200 an hour, see Bitrix24 development .
Post-launch support is easier to manage as a separate agreement or annex covering the hours package, how requests are submitted and the response time. Our packages are 5 hours for AED 1,250 a month, 10 hours for AED 2,300 and 20 hours for AED 4,200, with extra hours at AED 250. The scope is on the Bitrix24 support page.

Page: https://makebiztechnologies.com/en/journal/bitrix24-crm-forms
Title: Bitrix24 CRM forms: website leads into deals | MakeBiz

Journal · Bitrix24
# Bitrix24 CRM forms: website leads straight into deals
A website lead that goes to an inbox first loses time and often its ad source. Bitrix24 CRM forms remove that step. Here is how to set up the form, tagging, routing and the first WhatsApp reply.
A Bitrix24 CRM form creates a lead, or a deal with a contact, the moment it is submitted: form fields fill the record, UTM tags from ads are stored in the deal, a rep is assigned in rotation and an automation rule sets a task or triggers the first WhatsApp touch. At MakeBiz Technologies forms are part of an implementation with the standard setup from AED 10,000, or built separately at AED 200 an hour, and connecting WhatsApp costs AED 500.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## A CRM form writes the lead straight into Bitrix24
A typical website form sends an email to a shared inbox. Someone then has to notice it, copy the phone number into the CRM and assign a rep. The lead can get lost at every step, and the ad source is lost almost every time.
A Bitrix24 CRM form works differently: you build it inside the portal, and every submission creates a CRM record right away. You can publish the form in several ways:
- embed it with a code snippet on any page, including sites not built on Bitrix24
- show it as a pop-up on a button click or after a delay
- add it to the website widget next to live chat and the callback request
- share it as a link in WhatsApp, an email or an ad
If leads come from your own site form or another system, they can be passed into the CRM through the REST API or webhooks, which is a job for Bitrix24 development .
## The CRM scheme decides what a submission creates
In the form settings you choose which records appear in the CRM after a submission. That choice shapes how your sales team works from then on.
| What the form creates | When it fits | What to decide
| Lead | Lots of unqualified enquiries that need screening before a deal | Who converts leads into deals, and how fast
| Deal and contact | Enquiries are almost always genuine and go straight into the pipeline | Which pipeline and which stage the deal lands in
| Deal, contact and company | B2B sales where the client's organisation matters | A company name field and duplicate checks
| Repeat enquiry | The client is already in the database | The duplicate rule: a new record or a link to the existing one
Form features depend on the Bitrix24 plan, so we check the plan before quoting.
If you sell several services, a separate form for each one works well: the deal lands in its own pipeline, and the rep knows what the enquiry is about before calling.
## UTM tags show which ad brought the lead
When a visitor arrives through a link with UTM tags, the CRM form saves them in the record: source, medium, campaign, ad content and keyword. It works for Google Ads and Meta ads alike, as long as the links in your ads are tagged the same way.
The rule is simple: agree on one tagging convention before ads go live. For example, utm_source is always google or meta, and utm_campaign matches the campaign name in the ad account. Then the CRM report shows not just "website leads" but which campaign brings deals and payments. BI analytics from AED 300 a month puts ads, CRM and revenue on one screen, and our news on three dashboards a sales manager checks shows which reports matter.
### We build forms that create deals on submit
Forms, UTM tags, routing and automation at AED 200 an hour, WhatsApp connection AED 500
Discuss the setup
## Lead routing is set in the form and in automation rules
The form itself names the responsible person. If you list several, leads are assigned to them in turn. For finer logic, add automation rules to the first pipeline stage:
- reassign the lead by condition: the client's language, emirate or the service picked in the form
- give the rep a task with a deadline, for example call back within 15 minutes
- alert the manager if the deal stage has not changed within a set time
- email the client a confirmation that the request was received
How pipeline, rules and channels fit together is explained on the Bitrix24 implementation in Dubai page.
## The WhatsApp reply goes out as a template on the official channel
In the UAE a client who fills in a form expects a WhatsApp message, not an email. There is one technical catch: a form submission does not open WhatsApp's 24-hour customer service window. Only a message from the client does. So the first message after a form goes out as a template approved by Meta in advance, through the official WhatsApp Business Platform. We compared the API with WhatsApp Web in our guide WhatsApp Business API or WhatsApp Web .
The channel connects to Bitrix24 open channels for AED 500 with us, plus the provider subscription (details on the WhatsApp in Bitrix24 page). If the provider's app supports sending a template from an automation rule, the first touch can be automatic. If not, a rule gives the rep a task to message the client. Once the client replies, the chat lands in the record and the rep continues in free text.
If a rep goes quiet, the AI sales manager steps in: the agent replies to the client when the rep does not and keeps an eye on the pipeline. How an agent sorts incoming messages is covered in our news on the AI agent in WhatsApp .
## Five fields are enough for a first enquiry
Every extra field is one more reason to abandon the form. For a first enquiry five fields usually do the job: name, phone with country code, email, the service they are interested in and preferred language (English or Russian). The rep can ask the rest on the call.
Three settings people often forget: mark required fields clearly, add consent to data processing as a separate field, and switch on spam protection from day one, or the CRM fills up with bots. Fields can also appear by condition, so a budget question shows up for one service only.
## A worked example: a real estate agency with three forms
A hypothetical Dubai real estate agency takes enquiries to buy, rent and value a property. We build three forms, each creating a deal in its own pipeline. UTM tags from ads are saved in the record, enquiries rotate between brokers, and a rule alerts the manager if a deal sits untouched for 15 minutes. If the forms, rules and tagging take, say, 8 hours, that is AED 1,600 at AED 200 an hour, plus AED 500 to connect WhatsApp. In a project with the standard setup from AED 10,000, forms are built together with the pipeline. All prices are on the pricing page .
## Questions and answers
**Can I embed a Bitrix24 CRM form on a site that is not built on Bitrix24?**
Yes. The form embeds with a code snippet on any site, shows as a pop-up or opens from a link.
**Does the form keep UTM tags?**
Yes. If the visitor came through a tagged link, the tags are saved in the lead or deal. Agree on one tagging convention for Google Ads and Meta in advance.
**How do I split leads between sales reps?**
List several responsible people in the form and leads go to them in turn. More complex rules, for example by language or service, are set with automation rules on the first pipeline stage.
**Can we message the client on WhatsApp right after the form?**
Yes, but the first message is a Meta-approved template sent through the official channel, because a form submission does not open the 24-hour window. Connecting WhatsApp to Bitrix24 costs AED 500 with us.
**How much does CRM form setup cost?**
In a project with the standard setup from AED 10,000, forms are built together with the pipeline. On their own they are AED 200 an hour, with the scope fixed in the quote before work starts.

Page: https://makebiztechnologies.com/en/journal/bitrix24-crm-analytics
Title: Why CRM reports lie and how to fix them | MakeBiz

Journal · Analytics
# Why CRM reports lie and how to fix them
A sales director opens the pipeline report and does not believe it: conversion jumps around and revenue does not match the accounts. The report is rarely the problem. The data going into it usually is.
CRM reports go wrong for four reasons: duplicate clients, empty key fields, vague pipeline stages and no rules on who fills in what and when. The fix starts with a portal audit, which MakeBiz Technologies bills at AED 200 an hour with the estimate fixed before we start. Once the data is clean, BI dashboards start at AED 300 a month, with the first 14 days free.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## A report shows exactly what your team typed in
CRM reports do not count sales, they count records of sales. If a rep creates the same client twice, skips the lead source or closes a deal a month after payment, the report counts exactly that. So "the report is broken" almost always turns out to be a problem inside deal records, not in the widget settings.
| What you see | What is wrong in the data | What to fix
| Conversion jumps or tops 100% | Deals created without a lead, or one lead converted twice | One entry route: lead, then deal, created by automation
| More clients than you have | Duplicate companies and contacts | Merge duplicates, one +971 phone format
| Source "not specified" | Reps type the source by hand | Source from the form, UTM tags and channel
| Revenue does not match the books | Amount not updated after a discount, part payments missing | Amount and payment from Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo
| Deals stuck for months | No closing rule, no time limit per stage | Mandatory loss reason, automation for stalled deals
| Sales cycle looks too short | "Paid" stage set retroactively or skipped | Stage dates recorded automatically, skipping restricted
MakeBiz Technologies summary of common CRM data problems, not tied to any specific company.
## Duplicates inflate the database and split client history
A duplicate appears when a client messages on WhatsApp and later calls from another number, or when two reps add the same company under slightly different names. The report sees two clients and two histories. In reality it is one buyer who already has two different quotes.
Bitrix24 can find and merge duplicates by phone, email and company name. A one-off clean-up will not last unless you close the door: a check when a record is created, one phone format, and no new company without a search. Who may merge or delete records is an access rights question, covered in our news piece on CRM access rights .
## Empty fields turn analytics into guesswork
An empty field is not a zero, it simply drops out of the report. If only some deals have a loss reason, your "why we lose clients" report draws conclusions for everyone from that subset.
Making every field mandatory does not help: reps will type anything just to save the deal. What works:
- keep the 5 to 7 fields you actually decide on
- require each one only at the stage where the information appears: amount at the quote stage, loss reason at closing
- fill in automatically whatever can come from a form, a call or an invoice
- drop fields nobody has opened in a quarter
## Every stage has to mean the same thing to everyone
For one rep "Negotiation" is the first call, for another it is an agreed contract. The stage report then shows habits, not your sales process. Give each stage an entry criterion you can check: "Quote sent" means a quote is attached, "Invoice issued" means the invoice exists in the CRM or your accounting system.
Keep as many stages as your client has real decisions, usually 5 to 8. If nobody can describe a stage in one sentence, merge it with the next. Restrict stage skipping, or stage-to-stage conversion stops meaning anything.
### Find out why your reports do not add up
A portal audit covering duplicates, fields, stages and automation. AED 200 an hour, estimate fixed before we start
Book an audit
## Automation enforces the rules, a PDF policy does not
A CRM policy in a shared folder gets read once. Rules built into the portal work every day, and Bitrix24 does this with standard tools:
- a task is created when a deal has not moved for a set period
- stage-specific required fields stop a deal moving on without the data
- source and UTM tags come from the form and channel, see our guide to Bitrix24 CRM forms
- the sales manager gets a summary of records with empty fields
Where automation falls short, an AI agent helps. The AI sales manager agent watches the pipeline, nudges a rep about a deal with no next step and replies to the client if the rep goes quiet. Agents connect to your CRM and messengers, and a demo on your own process is free and takes 30 to 40 minutes.
## Fixing the data takes five steps
- Audit. We list the reports management needs and check them against fields, stages and automation, see the Bitrix24 audit page
- Clean-up. Merge duplicates, restore key fields from history, close dead deals with a reason
- Rules. Stage criteria, required fields, control automation, one phone format
- Accounting link. Amounts and payments come from your accounting system, so CRM revenue matches the books
- Dashboards. Only now do we build reports you can trust
The work is billed at AED 200 an hour, with the estimate fixed before we start. To keep things tidy after launch, a support plan covers 5 hours a month for AED 1,250 or 10 hours for AED 2,300. The accounting link is on the integrations page, all prices are on our pricing page .

Built-in Bitrix24 reports cover a rep's daily work. Management usually wants period comparisons, plan versus actual, ad spend and accounting on one screen. That is what BI analytics is for: Basic at AED 300 a month for up to 3 users, Standard at AED 700, Pro at AED 1,000, first 14 days free. Paying for 6 months saves 10%, a year saves 20%.
Which screens to start with is in our news piece on three dashboards a sales director checks . Clean data is also the base for a sales forecast from CRM data and end-to-end analytics from ad click to payment.
## A worked example: a distributor with 15 reps
A hypothetical Dubai distributor has used Bitrix24 for two years. Conversion looks high, CRM revenue does not match the books and loss reasons are rarely recorded. The audit finds that reps bypass leads, do not update amounts after discounts, and paid deals sit in the "Invoice" stage for weeks.
The company merges duplicates, keeps 6 stages with clear criteria, makes the loss reason mandatory, links amounts to accounting and only then adds dashboards for the managing director and two department heads.
## Questions and answers
**Why does my Bitrix24 conversion report show odd numbers?**
Usually deals are created without going through leads, or the same client exists several times. Reports count records, so start with how leads come in and with duplicates.
**How do I remove duplicates in Bitrix24?**
Built-in duplicate search finds matches by phone, email and company name, and you can merge them. To stop them coming back, use one phone format and check for an existing record before creating a new one.
**How many fields should be mandatory?**
Usually the 5 to 7 fields you make decisions on. Require them at the stage where the information appears and fill the rest automatically.

Title: BI implementation: stages, timeline and roles | MakeBiz

Journal · Analytics
# BI implementation: stages, timeline and roles
BI pays off when management makes decisions from it every day. Here is how to get from questions to working dashboards, and who owns what in the project.
BI implementation runs in five stages: management questions, data sources, data model and clean-up, dashboards, and adoption. MakeBiz BI plans cost AED 300, 700 and 1,000 a month (Basic up to 3 users, Standard up to 10, Pro unlimited), the first 14 days are free, and paying for 6 months saves 10%, for a year 20%.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## A BI project starts with management questions, not charts
The classic mistake is to build a good-looking dashboard first and look for an audience later. A month on, nobody opens it, because it answers no real business question. Start the other way round: the owner writes down 10 to 15 questions they want answered every day or every week.
- how much money came in this month and how much is still in the pipeline
- which rep is behind plan, and why
- which sources bring clients who actually pay
- where deals get stuck the longest
- which clients have stopped buying
Each question becomes a metric with a precise definition. "Revenue" has to mean the same thing to sales and finance: paid invoices or won deals, gross or net of 5% VAT. Until that is agreed, every chart will be disputed.
## Implementation runs in five stages
Each stage has a clear output, and the next one does not start without it.
| Stage | What happens | Output | Who is involved
| 1. Questions and metrics | Collect management questions, define the metrics | Metric list with formulas | Owner, head of sales
| 2. Sources | Map where the data lives, grant access | Source map | Data owner, IT
| 3. Model and clean-up | Link tables, remove duplicates, align reference lists | Data you can trust | Contractor and data owner
| 4. Dashboards | Build views by role: owner, sales head, marketing | Working screens on live data | Contractor, key users
| 5. Adoption | Bring the screens into weekly meetings, set up alerts | Decisions made from the dashboard | Management
MakeBiz Technologies stage plan. For a small company, stages 1 and 2 can fit into one meeting.
## Your data sources set the scope of work
The more systems you connect, the more work there is and the higher the risk of mismatches. So sources go in one at a time, starting with the main one.
- CRM. Deals, leads, reps, tasks. In MakeBiz BI, Bitrix24 data and Bitrix24 telephony are included in the subscription
- Accounting. Invoices and payments from Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo, connected on request for an extra fee
- Ads and web analytics. Spend and clicks for end-to-end analytics, also on request for an extra fee
- External telephony. If calls run through a separate provider rather than Bitrix24
- Spreadsheets. Plans and lists that live nowhere else. Move them into the CRM, or the report depends on whoever last edited the file
If accounting and the CRM are not yet linked, start with the integration: the invoice is raised from the deal, the payment flows back, and BI gets one chain instead of two. We integrate Bitrix24 with accounting from AED 10,000, see our integrations page . What to check with your phone provider is covered in our news on UAE telephony for your CRM .

## The data model matters more than the visuals
The data model is the set of rules that links tables: which deal belongs to which client, which invoice to which deal, which rep owns what. Get the model wrong and the neatest chart shows the wrong number.
This is where old CRM problems surface: duplicate companies, deals with no amount, reps who left but still appear in reports, amounts in different currencies. Everything is brought to AED and to one list of reps and business lines. We cover these errors in our guide on why CRM reports lie . If nobody has reviewed the portal in a while, start with a Bitrix24 audit , and if the pipeline does not match how you sell, you need CRM setup from AED 10,000.
## The project has four roles
- Project owner. The owner or MD who signs off questions and metrics, then actually uses the dashboard
- Data owner. Someone inside the company who knows where everything lives and enforces CRM data rules
- Key users. Head of sales, marketing, finance: they test the screens against their own work
- Contractor. MakeBiz connects the sources, builds the model and dashboards, and keeps them running
Access and data stay with you, the contract is with MakeBiz Technologies FZE LLC and invoices are in AED. A BI project stalls when there is no data owner: nobody fixes CRM errors, and the dashboard slowly loses trust.

# CRM for a B2B trading company in the UAE: long deals and accounting
In a trading company a deal runs for weeks, the client has several people involved, and the invoice comes out of the accounting system. A simple enquiry, call, payment pipeline does not cope with that.
A B2B trading company in the UAE needs a CRM where each client company has several contacts, deals move through stages from enquiry to payment, and quotes are built from a catalog. In Bitrix24 this is covered by standard setup from MakeBiz Technologies starting at AED 10,000 and going live from 14 days. Integration with Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo starts at AED 10,000 on top, with the estimate fixed before we start.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## A long B2B deal needs its own stages
In retail a customer decides within a day. In B2B trading, weeks pass between the first enquiry and payment: clarifying the spec, sending a quote, agreeing the price, sometimes a tender, then the contract, the invoice and the delivery. Squeeze all of that into three stages and deals sit in "Negotiation" for weeks while nobody can tell where an order is really stuck.
Build stages around the buyer's decisions, and give each one an entry criterion and an owner. A typical setup for a trading company:
| Stage | What the CRM records | What to automate
| Enquiry | Company, contact, channel, product and volume | Lead from email, form or WhatsApp, task for the rep
| Qualification | Volume, timing, decision maker, budget | Required fields before moving on
| Quote sent | Quote built from the catalog, version, validity date | Reminder if the client goes quiet
| Approval | Discount, payment and delivery terms, who approved | Manager sign-off for discounts above a threshold
| Contract and invoice | Contract, AED invoice with 5% VAT, client entity | Invoice from accounting, status in the deal
| Delivery and payment | Delivery date, part payments, balance due | Payment follow-up task on the due date
MakeBiz Technologies template for a trading company, adjusted to your process.
Repeat orders from existing clients work well in a separate pipeline: they have a different cycle and different tasks. Mix deal types in one pipeline and conversion reports stop making sense, see our guide on why CRM reports lie .
## In B2B the client is a company with several contacts
One buyer usually means several people: a procurement officer asking for prices, an engineer checking the spec, a finance team that pays and a director who signs. If the CRM holds a single contact, your rep is missing half the conversation.
In Bitrix24 every contact is linked to the company, and the deal shows who plays which role. Add the fields that matter in the UAE: the client's legal entity, its TRN for invoices, and whether it sits in a free zone or on the mainland. Running several of your own entities in one portal is covered in our news piece on free zone and mainland in one Bitrix24 .
Email belongs in the record too. Connect shared and personal mailboxes, and messages attach to the company and the deal.
## Quotes come from the catalog, not from Word
When reps put quotes together by hand, prices, SKUs and terms drift apart. In the CRM a quote is built from the product catalog: line items, AED prices, discount, 5% VAT on its own line, validity date. Every version is saved in the deal, so a month later you can see exactly what the client received.
For more involved approvals (a special price request, a credit limit check, a contract with custom terms) smart processes do the job. When you need them is explained in our guide to Bitrix24 smart processes , and custom work is on the Bitrix24 development page.

## Accounting holds the money, the CRM shows it
A common mistake in trading companies is tracking invoices and payments in both the CRM and the accounting system. Within a quarter the numbers diverge and nobody knows which to trust. The working model is simpler: the invoice is issued in accounting, and the CRM receives its number, amount and payment status.
Between Bitrix24 and Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo you would typically sync:
- the client list with company details
- products, prices and stock, if your accounting system holds them
- invoices and their status: issued, part paid, paid
- receivables for each client

Regular clients in trading reorder again and again, and the CRM makes sure you do not miss the moment. An automation rule creates a task when a client has gone longer than usual without ordering, and an overdue invoice triggers a reminder with the balance pulled from accounting.
Where reps cannot keep up, AI agents step in. The AI sales manager agent watches the pipeline and replies to the client if a rep goes quiet, and the call agent scores every conversation. # CRM for a car service centre in the UAE: bookings, servicing and WhatsApp
A garage rarely loses money in the bay. It loses it before: a missed call, a booking in a notebook, a customer nobody reminded about their next service. That is exactly where a CRM helps.

## A garage loses customers before the car reaches the bay
A service centre makes its money in the bay and loses it earlier. A call at rush hour goes unanswered. A WhatsApp message gets read and forgotten. A booking is scribbled in a notebook, and the technician finds out about the car when it is already at the gate. And the customer who came in six months ago goes elsewhere for the next service because nobody reminded them.
A CRM for a car service centre closes exactly these gaps: every enquiry lands in the system, every booking has a time slot and a bay, and every car has a service history and a next visit date. Here is the customer journey and what the CRM does at each step.
| Step | What the CRM does | Channel
| Enquiry | Creates a lead and finds the customer and car by phone number | Call, WhatsApp, website
| Booking | Puts the visit into the bay and technician calendar | Service advisor or online form
| Visit reminder | Sends a confirmation the day before | WhatsApp template
| Check-in | Records mileage, complaints, photos and a first estimate | Vehicle record
| Extra work | Sends the estimate for approval and logs the answer | WhatsApp
| Handover and payment | Closes the job card and passes the amount to accounting | Till, accounting system
| Next service | Schedules a reminder by date or mileage | WhatsApp template, task
MakeBiz Technologies template for a car service centre, adjusted to your process.
## The vehicle record matters more than the customer record
A garage works with cars, not just people. One customer may own two cars, and a corporate fleet can have dozens of vehicles and several drivers. The car is linked to a person or a company, so the service advisor types in a phone number and instantly sees which car it is, what was replaced last time and which work the customer postponed. An online form on your website creates a booking request, the service advisor confirms the slot, and the customer gets a WhatsApp message. The day before, the CRM sends a reminder, which cuts down on no-shows. Walk-ins go into the CRM too: the advisor creates the visit at check-in, so the car keeps its history and your capacity reports reflect reality.

# How to train your team to work with AI agents
An agent can be set up flawlessly and still go nowhere if the team does not understand what it does and where their own job starts. Training here is about how people and the agent split the work, not about buttons.
Train the team by role over the first 2 weeks after launch: who owns the agent, who checks its decisions, who works with its output and how mistakes get reported. At MakeBiz Technologies a demo of the agent on your process is free and takes 30 to 40 minutes, team training in Bitrix24 costs AED 200 an hour, and after launch the agent is looked after under the support plan at 10% of the implementation cost per month.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## Teams learn to share work with the agent, not to click buttons
An agent is not ordinary software. It messages clients, sets tasks and scores calls on its own, so every employee needs to know what the agent has already done, what it has left for them and when to step in.
That is why the first training topic is the process map, not the interface: which steps the agent now handles, which ones stay with people, and where the handovers are. Without that map, reps either duplicate the agent or stop watching what it does. We covered both mistakes in our news piece on five reasons AI agent projects stall .
## Every role has its own area of responsibility
We split the team into four roles. In a small company one person can cover two of them, but keep the responsibilities clearly separate.
| Role | Usually | What they do with the agent | What we train
| Agent owner | Head of department or process owner | Decides what the agent does alone and what needs approval | Reading agent reports, changing rules, settling edge cases
| Reviewer | Sales manager, team lead, accountant | Checks the agent's decisions in the first weeks | Where to see the agent's actions, how to flag a mistake
| User | Sales reps, buyers, recruiters | Works with what the agent has prepared | Reading suggestions, taking over a chat, not doubling up
| CRM admin | In-house admin or partner | Looks after access and integrations | Permissions, fields, where the agent writes its output
MakeBiz Technologies role split for agent launches, November 2026.
Name one person who signs off on the agent's rules. If anyone can change them, within a month the agent gives clients inconsistent answers and nobody remembers who changed what. Log every change in the playbook with a date and a reason.
## Ground rules are written down before launch
Verbal agreements turn into "I thought the agent would handle that" within a week. A short playbook of one or two pages clears up most questions. It should cover:
- what the agent does without approval, such as answering a standard question about delivery times or sending a meeting reminder
- what needs a human to confirm: a discount, a price change, a promised deadline, saying no to a client
- how an employee takes a conversation over from the agent and hands it back
- where to report an agent mistake and how quickly someone responds
- what data the agent must not see or forward
Write the playbook in the team's language. In Dubai that is often English and Russian at the same time, so we prepare both versions, just as we do for Bitrix24 team training .
### We will train your team to work with the agent
Roles, a playbook and a review of mistakes over the first 2 weeks, on your own portal. Training AED 200 an hour, agent demo free
Talk about training
## The first two weeks follow a plan
The first 10 working days are the most sensitive. Here is the plan we use as a starting point:
- Days 1 to 2. Short sessions by role: the process map, the playbook, where to see the agent's actions. Separate sessions for reps and for managers
- Days 3 to 5. The agent goes live and the reviewer checks every decision it makes and flags errors. Reps practise taking over conversations
- Days 6 to 7. First review: which mistakes repeat, and what to fix in the agent's rules and wording
- Days 8 to 9. Checks narrow down to edge cases and anything involving money
- Day 10. Wrap-up: what the agent now does on its own, what stays with people, and who owns the rules from here
Track three simple numbers over this period: how many agent decisions were checked, how many were corrected, and how often reps took a conversation over. If corrections are not going down, the cause is usually the rules or the source data, not the people.
The full path, with data, access and budget, is laid out in our guide to an AI adoption plan for the first 90 days . Team training is part of that plan, not a separate project.
## Quality control runs on reviewing mistakes
Agent mistakes in the first weeks are normal. Nobody hearing about them is not. Every mistake needs a route: an employee flags it, the reviewer checks it, the owner decides whether to change a rule or the wording. Once fixed, it should not come back.
Run this review in the CRM: the agent logs its actions in the deal record, and the reviewer sees them next to the conversation. In sales that is the AI sales manager , for calls it is the call speech analytics agent that scores every conversation. How to coach reps using those scores is covered in our guide on sales call analysis .
## Openness beats orders when people push back
A common fear is that the agent is there to watch staff or replace them. What helps is a plain explanation: the agent takes the routine, the decisions stay with people.
- show which tasks move to the agent and how much time they used to take
- give reps the right to take over a conversation at any moment
- share the agent's mistakes as openly as you review people's mistakes
- collect the team's suggestions and put them into the rules
Talk separately to your most experienced people. Their knowledge of how the process really works is what the agent's rules need, and when they help shape the setup, the team accepts the agent more calmly.
## A worked example: a sales team of 12
A hypothetical Dubai company connected an agent that replies on WhatsApp when a rep is too slow. In the first days reps kept duplicating its replies and clients got two messages. After the role sessions the team adopted one rule: if the agent has replied, the rep continues the conversation instead of starting over. The sales manager reviewed the agent's replies for two weeks, then kept checks only for discounts and deadlines.
Training for a team like this is billed at AED 200 an hour or covered by a support plan from AED 1,250 a month, see the Bitrix24 support and pricing pages. You can pick an agent for your process on the AI agents page.
## Questions and answers
**How long does it take a team to get used to an agent?**
Our baseline plan covers the first 2 weeks: role sessions, checking every decision, reviewing mistakes and then narrowing the checks. After that the agent runs as normal and the owner maintains the rules.
**Who in the company should own the agent?**
The process owner, usually the head of the department. They decide what the agent does alone and settle edge cases.
**Does everyone need the same training?**
No, training is by role: reps learn to take over conversations and not duplicate the agent, managers learn to read reports and change rules, the admin looks after access. We also split groups by language.
**How much does team training cost?**
A demo of the agent on your process is free and takes 30 to 40 minutes. Team training in Bitrix24 is AED 200 an hour or part of a support plan from AED 1,250 a month, prices exclude VAT.
**What if staff do not trust the agent?**
Show which tasks it takes over and give people the right to step in at any time. An open review of the agent's mistakes eases tension faster than any pep talk.

# AI sales assistant: what it does and what it costs
UAE customers message you on WhatsApp in the evening and expect an answer right away, while your sales rep is in a meeting or already home. An AI sales assistant covers those gaps and keeps an eye on your deals. Here is what it does, what it does not do and what goes into the budget.
An AI sales assistant drafts replies to customers on WhatsApp and other channels, answers on its own when a rep stays silent, tracks deals with no next step, creates tasks and reviews every conversation each morning. At MakeBiz Technologies this is the AI sales manager agent inside Bitrix24: AED 5,000 one-off to implement, support at 10% a month (AED 500), WhatsApp connection AED 500, with the provider subscription billed separately.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## The assistant works in the chat, in the deal and in a morning review
"AI sales assistant" can mean anything from a website chatbot to an email writer. A useful one sits inside your CRM and messengers and covers three areas: customer conversations, deal progress and team oversight.
| Task | What the assistant does | What the rep does
| Reply to a customer | Drafts a reply in the chat window with an AED price and a next step | Send, edit or rewrite it
| Silence in a chat | If the rep has not replied in 15 minutes, answers itself and creates a task | Pick the conversation back up
| "Waiting for reply" queue | Shows which customers are waiting and for how long, across all channels | Work through the queue
| Stalled deals | Finds deals with no next step and creates tasks | Contact the customer
| Who to call today | A list of customers with the reason and a suggested opener | Make the calls
| Chat review | Every morning: where reps slipped, which leads were closed too early, who to win back | Adjust the approach
Functions of the MakeBiz Technologies AI sales manager agent in Bitrix24.
## The WhatsApp reply is ready before the rep opens the chat
The assistant reads the conversation, the customer record and your knowledge base: price list, terms, answers to common questions. From that it drafts a reply right in the chat window. The rep pastes it, edits it, or asks for a shorter or softer version with one click. In the evening and during meetings, the fallback kicks in: if the rep is silent for 15 minutes, the agent replies to the customer using an agreed script and creates a task for the owner of the deal.
The limits are set in advance: the assistant does not offer discounts, does not promise unconfirmed dates and does not argue. Unusual requests, complaints or "can I talk to a person" go straight to a rep. How the agent handles first messages from ads is covered in our news piece on the AI agent in WhatsApp .
All of this needs the official channel: one company number connected to the CRM. Connecting WhatsApp to Bitrix24 costs AED 500, the scope is on our messengers in Bitrix24 page, and the difference between the official API and WhatsApp Web is explained in our guide WhatsApp Business API or WhatsApp Web .
## Deal follow-up runs on rules you define
Deals are lost in the gaps: the quote went out, the customer went quiet, nobody set a next step. The assistant checks the pipeline against rules you write down:
- every open deal has a next step with a date
- if a customer has not replied a set number of days after a quote, a task appears
- a deal that sits in one stage longer than normal goes on the manager's list
Simple conditions can be handled by standard CRM automation rules too. The difference is text: the agent reads the chat, understands that the customer wrote "let us pick this up after the holidays" and sets the task for the right date. When you need a rule and when you need an agent is explained on our AI in Bitrix24 page, and the full feature list is on the AI sales manager page.

WhatsApp replies, chat fallback and deal follow-up in Bitrix24. AED 5,000 to implement, the demo is free
Book a demo
## A morning chat review replaces spot checks
A sales manager cannot read every conversation from the day, so they usually check a few at random. The assistant reviews all of them and has a short summary ready by morning: where a rep ignored the customer's question, which leads were marked lost too early, who is worth winning back and what to say. Next to it sit plan versus actual for each rep and the deals to close first.
Calls are handled by a separate agent: call speech analytics scores every conversation. It is priced by minutes: 5,000 minutes a month cost AED 1,000, and 10,000 minutes cost AED 1,700.

- CRM: if Bitrix24 is not set up yet, standard setup starts from AED 10,000 and takes from 14 days, see our Bitrix24 implementation page
Prices exclude licences and VAT, and the estimate is fixed before work starts. The full price list is on our pricing page . Before any implementation we show the agent on your own process for free, and the demo takes 30 to 40 minutes.
## The assistant does not sell for your reps
AI saves time around the deal: replies, record updates, reminders, reviews. It does very little for the deal itself: price, discount, contract terms and trust in a person stay with your rep. We go through that maths in our news piece on where AI in sales saves time and where it does not .
For the assistant to work you need three things: one business number in the CRM instead of personal phones, a defined pipeline with clear stages, and a knowledge base with prices and terms. Which agent to start with if your sales team is new to AI is covered in our news piece on the first agent for a sales team .
## A worked example: an equipment supplier with 10 reps
A hypothetical Dubai equipment supplier gets WhatsApp leads from ads, including evenings and weekends. Some messages wait until morning and deals stall after the quote. After launch the reply is ready in the chat window, overnight messages get a first answer from the script, and each morning the manager sees the review and a list of who to call. ## Questions and answers
**How is an AI sales assistant different from a chatbot?**
A chatbot follows a fixed script. The assistant sees the conversation, the deal record and your knowledge base, drafts a reply for that specific customer, tracks deals and hands complex cases to a rep.
**Will the assistant reply to customers at night?**
Yes. If the rep has not replied, the agent answers using an agreed script and creates a task for the deal owner. It does not promise discounts or unconfirmed dates.
**Do we need Bitrix24 for the assistant?**
The AI sales manager works inside Bitrix24 and your messengers. If you have no CRM yet, we set up the portal first: standard setup starts from AED 10,000 and takes from 14 days.

Implementing the AI sales manager agent is AED 5,000 one-off, with support at 10% of that per month, so AED 500. Connecting WhatsApp is AED 500, and the provider subscription and Meta fees are separate.
**Can the manager see what the assistant said?**
Yes. Every reply from the assistant is logged in the Bitrix24 deal next to the reps' messages. The manager sees where the agent stepped in and which task it created.

# AI automation beyond sales: finance, procurement and hiring
Most talk about AI in business is about sales: reply to the lead, score the call. Yet a lot of repetitive work lives in the back office, and agents take the grind out of it there too. Here is what each department can hand to an agent and what stays with people.
Beyond sales, AI agents take over repetitive work in finance, procurement and hiring: a view of cash and risk by business line, supplier requests and quote comparison, and the first interview with a candidate. At MakeBiz Technologies one such agent costs AED 5,000 one-off, a team of agents for several departments AED 10,000, and support is 10% of the implementation fee per month.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## The back office runs on repeatable work
Every week your finance person pulls numbers from the accounting system and the CRM into one spreadsheet. Your buyer sends the same request to five suppliers and then copies their answers by hand. Your recruiter asks the first candidates the same ten questions. That is template work, and an agent can take the longest part of it while leaving the decision with a person.
| Department | Task | What the agent does | What stays with people
| Finance | Cash picture by business line | Pulls together revenue, costs, profit and balances, flags risks | Decisions on payments, budgets and credit
| Procurement | Supplier requests and quote comparison | Sends requests, collects replies, compares price, lead time and reliability | Choosing the supplier and negotiating
| Hiring | Initial candidate screening | Takes in applications, runs the first interview, scores and tracks the pipeline | Final interview and offer
| Marketing | Content and search visibility | Drafts articles and tracks visibility in search and AI assistants | Positioning and sign-off
| Client relationships | Who is waiting and who needs a follow-up | Surfaces forgotten contacts and people awaiting a reply | The conversation and the relationship
Task scope of MakeBiz Technologies agents, November 2026. The exact feature set for your process is fixed in the estimate.
## The finance agent builds the cash picture
A managing director wants revenue, profit, costs and cash runway for every business line on one screen, not a report at month end. The finance agent builds that view from your accounting system and CRM, calculates margin and profitability, and raises a flag when something drifts: a business line turns negative, costs run ahead of plan, or cash covers a shorter period than usual.
The agent does not pay or sign anything. It saves time on collecting numbers and shows you where to look. For the data to flow on its own, the CRM must be linked to accounting: our Bitrix24 integration with Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Odoo starts at AED 10,000. The management dashboards themselves live in BI analytics , with plans from AED 300 a month.
## The procurement agent puts every quote in one table
In procurement the time goes on correspondence. You send the request, wait for replies, chase the suppliers who went quiet, and move prices from PDFs and emails into a spreadsheet. The procurement agent sends requests to suppliers, collects their quotes and compares them on price, lead time and reliability. Your buyer gets a ready comparison and spends the time negotiating instead of copying.
The costliest comparison mistakes hide in the details: different currencies, VAT included or on top, different delivery terms. We covered them in our news piece on where money leaks when comparing suppliers . And for why even accurate document recognition does not stop invoice errors, read our news on 98% accuracy .

## The HR agent runs the first interview
A single vacancy in Dubai can attract more applications than a recruiter has time to read. The first call with each candidate takes time, and half of them drop out on basics: experience, languages, availability for the schedule, salary expectations. The HR agent takes applications from job boards and your website, runs the first interview on WhatsApp or Telegram, scores the answers and moves each candidate through the pipeline up to their first day.
Your recruiter sees a shortlist with a score for every candidate. The final interview, the decision and the offer stay with people. Candidates who are not a fit right now go into a talent pool instead of getting lost in chat threads.
## Marketing and client relationships can run on agents too
Two agents sit next to sales but do not work on a specific deal. The marketing agent drafts and publishes articles and tracks how visible the company is in search and in AI assistants. The relationship agent keeps the full picture of your contacts: who is waiting for a reply, who you have not spoken to in a while, who needs a nudge. Both make sense once the core processes are already automated.
## Start with the department where work repeats daily
Pick the department not by what sounds exciting but by three signs: the task repeats every day, mistakes cost money, and the result can be measured with a number. In procurement that is the time from request to supplier choice, in hiring the time to first interview, in finance how quickly the director gets the cash picture.
Before launch, make sure the agent will have something to work with:
- finance needs access to the accounting system and CRM, plus the list of business lines to report profit on
- procurement needs a supplier list, a request template and comparison rules: currency, VAT, lead times
- hiring needs a job description, first-round questions and the criteria for moving a candidate forward
If agents need to work together, say procurement hands an upcoming payment to finance, they need shared data. That is the Business package at AED 10,000: a team of agents, a shared dashboard and a phased rollout.
