Title: Where an AI agent fits into a business process | MakeBiz

Journal · AI agents
# Where an AI agent fits into a business process
An AI agent does not replace a whole process. It slots into specific steps, while CRM automation and people keep handling the rest. Here is how to map a process so each step goes to whoever handles it most reliably and at the lowest cost.
An AI agent belongs on the steps where someone has to understand free text, speech or a document and decide by set rules: the first reply to a client, qualifying a lead from a chat, scoring a call, a summary for the manager. Steps with a clear trigger go to CRM automation, while money, exceptions and disputes stay with a person. At MakeBiz Technologies one agent costs AED 5,000, and CRM automation is set up at AED 200 an hour.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## Every process has three kinds of steps
Write down every step from first enquiry to payment. Nearly all fall into three groups: an action that follows a rule, an action that requires understanding, and a decision someone is accountable for. The group decides who should do the step.
| Process step | Who does it | Why
| A website form becomes a lead in the CRM | CRM automation | A fixed rule: create the lead and record the source
| A client messages on WhatsApp in the evening | AI agent | It has to understand the question and answer from the knowledge base
| Assigning the account manager | CRM automation | Routing by queue, language or team
| Qualification: need, budget, timing | AI agent | The answers are buried in free-text chat
| A discount above the limit | Person | Money and responsibility for margin
| Scoring a call against criteria | AI agent | It means analysing speech, not reading a field
| An invoice from a template once terms are agreed | CRM automation | All the data is already in the deal record
| A summary of stalled deals | AI agent | It has to pick what matters and explain why a deal is stuck
| A disputed client complaint | Person | The relationship and a decision on behalf of the company
MakeBiz Technologies mapping for a typical sales process. In your process the steps and their owners may differ.
## CRM automation takes every if-then step
If a step can be written as "when the deal moves to stage X, do Y", it does not need AI. Creating a lead from a form, setting a task, sending a template email, moving the stage after payment: that is the job of Bitrix24 automation rules and workflows. A rule fires the same way every time, costs less and does not slip on simple things.
An agent on such a step is paying for understanding where there is nothing to understand. We explained the difference between the two tools in our news piece on AI agents versus CRM automation . When standard rules are not enough, custom scenarios and links to outside systems are built through Bitrix24 development at AED 200 an hour.
## An agent steps in where meaning matters
You need an agent on the steps where the input does not fit into a field: a client message, a conversation, a supplier email, a document. A rule cannot tell that "would it be cheaper if we signed for a year?" signals interest in an annual contract. An agent can, answers from the knowledge base and notes in the deal record what the client is after.
Typical places for an agent in a sales process:
- the first reply to a client when the rep goes quiet, plus pipeline control: that is the AI sales manager
- scoring every conversation against criteria instead of a sample: that is the call agent
- sorting incoming enquiries in a messaging app: we described how it works in our news on the AI agent in WhatsApp
Some of these tasks are covered by the AI built into Bitrix24, which transcribes calls and fills in fields. Where that is enough and where you need a separate agent is explained on our AI-powered CRM page.
### Let us map your process together
We will show where you need an agent and where CRM automation will do. Free 30 to 40 minute demo, one agent from AED 5,000
Book a demo
## A person stays where mistakes are expensive
Some steps belong to neither automation nor an agent: a discount above the limit, non-standard payment terms, a disputed complaint. A person decides here, because a person answers for the outcome.
The agent's job on these steps is different: spot that the situation has gone outside the rules and bring in the right colleague with a short summary. The manager gets the essence rather than the raw chat: what the client wants, what has already been promised, how much is at stake. The decision stays with them, it just happens faster.
## The agent's limits are set before launch
Before launch every agent gets three lists: what it can read, what it can change and what it must never do. For example, the agent may reply to clients and update qualification fields, but cannot change the deal amount and never promises discounts. Everything it does is visible in the deal record.
The agent runs under its own user account with the right permissions. Access and data stay with your company, and if the agent replies on a messaging channel, that channel is connected the official way: we connect WhatsApp to Bitrix24 for AED 500, details on our messaging page .
## One working session is enough to map the process
Mapping does not need a long project. You can do it in a single meeting with the process owner:
- List the steps from first contact to payment as they happen today, not as they were designed
- Tag each step: rule, meaning or decision
- Mark where things fall through most often: unanswered enquiries, calls nobody reviews, deals that do not move
- Put an agent on one narrow step that needs understanding, and hand the rest to automation
- Decide which number will show the result: response time, share of calls reviewed
With that map the budget is easier to plan. What it is made of is covered in our guide to AI agent scope and pricing , and how to run the first quarter in our 90-day AI adoption plan .
## A worked example: a service company taking WhatsApp enquiries
A hypothetical air-conditioning maintenance company in Sharjah gets most of its enquiries on WhatsApp. Evening enquiries wait until morning, and CRM automation only creates the lead.
After mapping, the process looks like this. Automation creates the lead and assigns a rep by area. The agent replies in the evening, asks for the address, the unit model and the problem, and records them in the deal. Automation books the visit in the calendar once the client confirms a time. A person handles only the exceptions: warranty disputes and discounts. Budget on our lines: AED 5,000 for the agent under Start, AED 500 a month for support and a few hours of automation work at AED 200 an hour. All agents are listed on the AI agents page .
## Questions and answers
**How is an AI agent different from CRM automation?**
Automation runs an action on a clear trigger: the stage changed, so create a task. An agent understands free text, speech and documents and makes decisions within the rules you give it.
**Can an agent run the whole process at once?**
Technically yes, but it is safer to start with one narrow step that needs understanding. Rule-based steps are cheaper and more stable in CRM automation.
**Which decisions should never go to an AI agent?**
Decisions about money and exceptions: discounts above the limit, non-standard payment terms, disputed complaints. The agent spots these cases and hands them to a person with a summary.
**How do I check what the agent is doing?**
Every action the agent takes is visible in the deal record, and its permissions are set in advance: what it reads, what it changes and what is off-limits. A manager reviews its work the same way as an employee's.
**How much does it cost to add an agent to a process?**
One agent under the Start package costs AED 5,000 one-off, with support at AED 500 a month. CRM automation around the agent is set up at AED 200 an hour, prices exclude VAT.

# AI adoption plan for a company: the first 90 days
AI projects rarely fail because of the technology. They stall on messy data, unclear access rights and nobody owning the result. This plan for your first quarter deals with those issues in order.
The first 90 days of AI adoption break down into three stages: preparing the process, data and access; piloting one agent; and deciding whether to scale. A one-agent pilot with MakeBiz Technologies costs AED 5,000 plus AED 500 a month for support, so our part of the quarter's budget stays within AED 6,500. You can start with a free 30 to 40 minute demo on your own process.
MakeBiz Technologies · 11 November 2026 · 7 min read
## The quarter splits into three 30-day stages
Ninety days is a framework, not a promised deadline. Each stage can run shorter or longer depending on the state of your CRM and data. What matters is that every stage has a clear output, and the next one does not start until the previous one is done.
| Period | What happens | Who owns it | Output
| Days 1-30 | Pick the process, name an owner, gather data and access | Process owner and MakeBiz | Process description, knowledge base, access list, baseline numbers
| Days 31-60 | Launch one agent working alongside the team | Process owner, team, MakeBiz | Agent in production, first error reviews
| Days 61-90 | Compare before and after, decide what comes next | Managing director or CEO | Decision: scale, tune or stop
MakeBiz Technologies framework for a one-agent pilot. Actual timings depend on how ready your data is and are fixed in the estimate.
## Choose the process by money, not by hype
Your first agent belongs where the work repeats every day and where dropping it costs money. Four questions help you choose:
- how many times a day or week does the task come up
- what does a mistake or delay cost: a lost lead, an overpaid supplier, a candidate who joined a competitor
- is there data the agent can rely on: the CRM, a price list, templates, chat history
- can the result be measured with one simple number: response time, share of unanswered leads, calls scored
For a sales team we covered the order of choice in our news piece on which agent to start with in sales . If sales already run smoothly, see our guide to AI in finance, procurement and hiring , which applies the same criteria to other departments.
## Name the owner before you start
Every agent needs an owner inside the company. Not an IT person, but whoever is accountable for the process: the head of sales, the procurement lead, the HR manager. They decide what the agent tells clients, where its permissions end and when a human steps in. Without that owner a pilot turns into an experiment nobody remembers a month later.
Two more roles matter. A CRM administrator opens access and looks after the fields. The managing director makes the call at the end of the quarter, based on the numbers. A missing owner is one of the reasons AI agent projects stall , so we pin these roles down in week one.
## Data and access are prepared in month one
An agent works with whatever data it is given. If your CRM is full of duplicates, empty fields and stages nobody uses, the agent will repeat that mess faster than people do. So the first month goes on preparation:
- Review the pipeline and fields in the CRM. If nobody has looked at the portal in a while, start with a Bitrix24 audit
- Build a knowledge base: price list, payment and delivery terms, answers to common questions, document templates
- Connect channels the official way. For WhatsApp that means the Business Platform; we connect it to Bitrix24 for AED 500, details on the messaging page
- Give the agent its own user account with the right permissions instead of running it under an employee's login
- Record baseline numbers so you have something to compare against
Access and data stay with your company. If you have no CRM yet, that comes first: a standard Bitrix24 setup starts at AED 10,000 with go-live from 14 days.
### Start with a demo on your own process
30 to 40 minutes, free. A one-agent pilot is AED 5,000 plus AED 500 a month for support
Book a demo
## The pilot runs alongside the team, not instead of it
In month two the agent goes live. For the first weeks it works in parallel with people. The AI sales manager , for example, only replies when a rep has gone quiet, and the call agent scores conversations that a manager would otherwise only spot-check. Your team sees how the agent makes decisions, and trust builds on evidence.
Every week the process owner and our team review the agent's mistakes: where it answered wrongly, where data was missing, where it should have called a human straight away. Those reviews are the real work of a pilot. The rules that come out of them go into the knowledge base, and the agent stops repeating the same slips.
## The quarter's budget is known upfront
Our share of the pilot budget is simple to work out. Implementing one agent under the Start package costs AED 5,000 one-off. Support is 10% of that, so AED 500 a month from launch. Across the quarter that comes to no more than AED 6,500.
CRM licences and the WhatsApp provider subscription are separate and paid to the vendors. If the pilot needs a CRM setup or an integration with your accounting system (Zoho Books, QuickBooks, Odoo), that work goes into the estimate before we start. Your contract is with MakeBiz Technologies FZE LLC, invoices are in AED and prices exclude VAT. All prices are on our pricing page , and what each package includes is explained in our guide to AI agent scope and pricing .
## Day 90 ends with one of three decisions
At the end of the quarter the managing director compares the numbers and chooses:
- scale : add agents in neighbouring departments under the Business package, AED 10,000 with shared data and a dashboard
- tune : the agent works but the numbers fell short, so another month goes on rules and data
- stop : the process was the wrong pick, the agent is switched off, and data and access stay with you
A worked example: a hypothetical Dubai service company with 12 staff loses enquiries that arrive on WhatsApp after 6 pm. In month one it cleans up the pipeline and builds a bank of answers, in month two it launches the AI sales manager, and in month three it sees how many evening enquiries got a reply and turned into deals. That number drives the decision. You can browse the agents that could come next on the AI agents page .
## Questions and answers
**Where should a company start with AI?**
Pick one process that repeats every day and costs money when it breaks, and name the person who owns it. Data and access are then prepared for that specific process.
**How much does an AI agent pilot cost?**
Implementing one agent with MakeBiz Technologies costs AED 5,000, with support at AED 500 a month. Over the first quarter our share comes to no more than AED 6,500, excluding VAT and licences.
**Who should be responsible for an AI agent?**
The process owner: the head of sales, the procurement lead or the HR manager. They decide what the agent says and where its limits are, while the CRM administrator handles access and fields.
**Do I need a CRM to deploy an AI agent?**
Our agents connect to the CRM and messaging channels, so without a system holding clients and deals they have nothing to work from. If you have no CRM, a standard Bitrix24 setup starts at AED 10,000.
**What if the pilot does not deliver?**
Find out why: the data, the rules or the choice of process. The agent can be tuned or switched off, and your data and access stay with your company either way.

Page: https://makebiztechnologies.com/en/journal/whatsapp-business-api-vs-whatsapp-web
Title: WhatsApp Business API or WhatsApp Web in your CRM | MakeBiz

Journal · Messaging
# WhatsApp Business API or WhatsApp Web in your CRM
In the UAE customers message you on WhatsApp, so it is one of the first channels a company connects to its CRM. There are two ways to do it: the official WhatsApp platform or a WhatsApp Web connector. Here is how they differ.
For a UAE sales team the official WhatsApp Business Platform (API) is the safer choice: one number for the whole team, conversations inside the client record, templates and clear limits. A WhatsApp Web connector relies on third-party software, and the WhatsApp terms for the Business App prohibit apps that interact with the service without WhatsApp's written consent. MakeBiz Technologies connects the channel to Bitrix24 for AED 500, Meta message fees are separate.
MakeBiz Technologies · 10 November 2026 · 7 min read
## The two options are different by design
The official platform is a business channel: your company number is verified by Meta and connected to the CRM through a provider. WhatsApp Web in a CRM is a workaround: a program or browser extension reads chats from the app on a phone and copies them into the portal.
| Criterion | WhatsApp Business Platform (API) | WhatsApp Web in a CRM
| How it connects | Through a provider, number verified by Meta | Third-party software attached to the phone app
| WhatsApp terms | Official channel for businesses | Business App terms prohibit such apps without written consent
| Team | One number, chats routed between reps | Depends on one app session staying alive
| First message to a client | A template approved by Meta | Free text, outside platform rules
| Broadcasts | The limit grows with message quality | Bulk sends put the number at risk
| Cost | Provider subscription plus Meta message fees | Cheap at first, expensive if the number is lost
MakeBiz Technologies comparison based on WhatsApp and Meta documents, checked 10 November 2026.
## WhatsApp's own terms settle the question
The WhatsApp Terms for WhatsApp Business App (effective 23 September 2026, section 5 "Restrictions") say a company must not develop or use any applications that interact with the Business App services without WhatsApp's prior written consent, and must not scrape or extract data from them. The same terms describe the app as designed for small to medium businesses.
A WhatsApp Web connector is exactly that kind of third-party app. It works fine until it does not. If the terms are breached the account can be restricted, and with the number the company loses the channel its clients know it by. That is a sales risk, not a matter of taste.
## The 24-hour window and templates come with the API
According to Meta's pricing documentation , a message from a customer opens a 24-hour customer service window. Inside it your rep replies in free text, outside it you can only send a template. Templates are approved by Meta in advance: a meeting reminder, an order status, an invoice.
For a CRM this means response speed has a price. In Bitrix24 we set up response time control: if a message has no reply for 15 minutes, the manager is notified while the window is still open. How an agent can sort incoming leads is covered in our news piece on the AI agent in WhatsApp .
Templates fall into categories: marketing, utility and authentication, while ordinary replies inside the window count as service messages. The category sets the price of a message, so name templates in the CRM in a way that lets a rep see at a glance which one is promotional and which one is for handling an order.
### We connect WhatsApp to Bitrix24 the official way
Company number, open channels, a lead from the first message and response time control. Connection AED 500
Connect WhatsApp
## Broadcast limits grow with quality
Meta's messaging limits page defines the limit as the number of unique WhatsApp users a business can message outside a customer service window in a moving 24-hour period. A newly created business portfolio starts at 250. Completing one of the scaling paths raises it to 2,000.
After that the limit rises automatically if messages across all your numbers and templates are high quality and you use at least half of your current limit over 7 days. That is why blasting a list of people who never opted in hurts twice: complaints lower your quality rating, and the limit goes down with it.
## What each option costs
The official channel has three budget lines:
- connection and setup in Bitrix24: AED 500 one-off with us, covering the number, open channels, routing and deal fields
- the API provider subscription: at the provider's rates
- Meta message fees: they depend on the market and the message category, and since 1 October 2026 service messages above 1,000 a month per number are charged too, see our news on WhatsApp Business pricing in the UAE
WhatsApp Web looks free, but the bill arrives later: time spent reconnecting, chats that never reached the CRM and the risk of losing the number. The full scope is on the WhatsApp and messengers in Bitrix24 page, and all prices are on the pricing page .
To see your own number in advance, export last month's outgoing messages from the portal and split them into templates and live replies from reps. That is quicker than guessing from the rate card.
## How to move from WhatsApp Web to the API
- Decide which number becomes the company number and export the chats you need from the app
- Pick an API provider and complete Meta's business verification
- Set up open channels: queue, working hours with UAE weekends, auto-reply
- Link chats to leads and deals and add response time control
- Get 3 to 5 templates approved: first message, reminder, invoice, status
- Tell clients if the number changes and switch off the old connector
The longest waits are usually business verification and template approval. That is why the old connector is switched off only once the new channel is live and the team is used to it, so sales do not stop during the move.
## A worked example: an agency with 8 sales reps
A hypothetical Dubai agency runs WhatsApp Web in its CRM: every rep works from their own phone and some chats never reach the portal. After moving to the API the agency has one number, chats are routed in turn, and the manager sees each rep's response time. One-off cost: AED 500 for the channel plus a few hours on automation and templates at AED 200 an hour.
## Questions and answers
**Can I connect WhatsApp Web to Bitrix24?**
Such connectors exist, but the WhatsApp terms for the Business App prohibit apps that interact with the service without WhatsApp's written consent. For a company the official platform is the safer route.
**How much does the WhatsApp Business API cost in the UAE?**
Connecting it to Bitrix24 is AED 500 one-off with us. The provider subscription and Meta message fees come on top, and the fees depend on the market and the message category.
**What is the 24-hour window in WhatsApp?**
A customer message opens a 24-hour customer service window in which you can reply in free text. Outside it a business can only send templates approved by Meta.
**How many messages can I send through the WhatsApp API?**
A new business portfolio can message 250 unique users in 24 hours outside the service window. It can be raised to 2,000, and after that it grows with message quality.
**Can several sales reps work with one number?**
Yes. With the API the company number is connected to Bitrix24 open channels, and chats are routed between reps by queue, language or team.

MakeBiz Technologies · 10 November 2026 · 7 min read
## Eight checks before you sign
Most of these take one call and one email. If a partner is vague on two or three of them, stop before the deposit, not after it.
| What to check | How | Red flag
| Partner status | Listing in the bitrix24.ae directory | No link, or "we work through a partner we know"
| Legal entity and contract | Company name, licence, draft contract | No contract, or a contract with an individual
| Currency and invoices | AED invoice issued to your company | Payment to a personal card, "USD at today's rate"
| Estimate | List of work, hours, hourly rate | One lump sum with no breakdown
| Access | Who owns the portal and accounts | Portal registered to the contractor
| Support | Monthly hour package, response time | "Just message us" with no terms
| Case studies | Task, result, industry | Logos with no detail
| Training | Plan by role: sales rep, manager, admin | One general video call after launch
MakeBiz Technologies checklist, 10 November 2026. It works for any partner, us included.
## Partner status is checked in the vendor directory
Official Bitrix24 partners in the region are listed in the partner directory on bitrix24.ae . Ask the contractor for the link to their listing and open it yourself. Going through a partner also makes it easier to buy and renew licences and to switch plans without losing data.
Status alone does not guarantee a good setup, but it filters out resellers who pass your project on to someone else. MakeBiz Technologies is an official Bitrix24 partner in the UAE, and the scope of our work is on the Bitrix24 implementation page.

For a UAE company it is simpler to work with a contractor that has a legal entity in the Emirates: a contract with a UAE company, invoices in dirhams, payment to a corporate account. Expenses are easier to book and disputes are easier to settle.
The estimate should show what the total is made of: standard setup, hourly custom work, integrations, training. All prices are on the pricing page . The Bitrix24 licence is paid separately, and we cover how to pick one in the guide on plans for 10, 25 or 50 users .
Ask separately how changes during the project are priced. The normal practice is that a new task is estimated in hours first, you approve the estimate in writing, and only then does the work start. If a partner is happy to make changes "as we go and settle up later", you will only learn the total at the end, when it is too late to argue about it.

## Access and data stay with your company
The portal, the WhatsApp number, telephony and integration accounts should all be registered to your company. The contractor works under a separate admin account that you can switch off in one click.
- the portal owner is your employee, not the contractor
- passwords to services stay with you, the contractor joins by invitation
- access is closed when the work ends, and the contract says so
If a partner offers to "register everything under us, it is faster", you risk losing your client history when you change contractors. The same questions apply to an AI vendor, and we listed them in the news piece on 7 questions to ask before signing .
## Support after launch matters more than a fast start
Teams ask for the most changes in the first two or three months: new fields, reports, automation rules, permissions. Ask up front how support works: an hour package, response time, who exactly answers. Our Bitrix24 support packages are AED 1,250, 2,300 and 4,200 a month for 5, 10 and 20 hours.

## A worked example: two quotes for the same job
Take a hypothetical trading company in Dubai with 15 sales reps that gets two quotes. The first says "CRM setup for AED 4,000" with no scope. The second lists a standard setup at AED 10,000 plus 15 hours for the website integration and reports at AED 200, AED 13,000 in total, with stages and a launch date.
The first looks cheaper until the change requests start: each one is billed separately and there is no contract with a scope of work. Three months later the totals are close, but the company has neither an estimate nor a clear portal owner. Compare the scope and terms from the table above, not the bottom line.
If you already have both quotes, put them side by side against the eight checks and ask each contractor to fill the empty cells in writing. The choice usually becomes obvious, and price stops being the only argument.

# Which Bitrix24 plan for 10, 25 or 50 users
Cloud Bitrix24 is not priced per user but per portal, with a user cap. So for 10, 25 and 50 people the answer is often the same plan, and the real question is which features you need.
For a team of 10, 25 or 50 people in the UAE, Standard usually fits: AED 364 a month billed annually for the whole portal of up to 50 users, or AED 4,368 a year. Basic at AED 180 covers only 5 people, and Professional at AED 731 a month (up to 100 users) is worth it when you need sales automation, call tracking and analytics tools. Prices from bitrix24.ae in US dollars, converted at AED 3.6725, checked on 10 November 2026.
MakeBiz Technologies · 10 November 2026 · 6 min read
## You pay for the portal, not for each person
A cloud Bitrix24 plan has a fixed price and a user cap: Basic 5, Standard 50, Professional 100, Enterprise 250 and up. A team of 10 pays the same for Standard as a team of 50, so the cost per person drops as you grow. The Free plan covers 1 to 2 users and is only good for a first look at the system.
| Team | Plan | Per month, billed annually | Per year | Per person per month
| 10 people | Standard | AED 364 ($99) | AED 4,368 | about AED 36
| 25 people | Standard | AED 364 ($99) | AED 4,368 | about AED 15
| 50 people | Standard | AED 364 ($99) | AED 4,368 | about AED 7
| 50 people with sales automation | Professional | AED 731 ($199) | AED 8,772 | about AED 15
| 51 to 100 people | Professional | AED 731 ($199) | AED 8,772 | from AED 7
Vendor prices from bitrix24.ae in US dollars as of 10 November 2026, converted at AED 3.6725, before promotions. Yearly total = monthly price × 12. All plans are on the Bitrix24 licences and prices page.
## Basic only fits a very small team
Basic is AED 180 a month billed annually and includes sales pipelines, recurring deals, online payments, and email, telephony and WhatsApp integration. But the cap is 5 users, so a sixth person will not fit. For a team of 10, Basic is off the table even if the features are enough.
It makes sense when the CRM is for the owner and two or three reps and the team will not grow within a year. If growth is planned, price Standard from the start: moving up a plan keeps your data, but permissions and automation for the bigger team still need a review.
## Standard covers most teams up to 50 people
On bitrix24.ae, Standard adds to Basic unlimited leads, invoices and estimates, a CRM form designer, e-signature, WhatsApp marketing, task KPIs, unlimited projects and 100 GB of storage. For a sales team that keeps clients, deals, chats and invoices in one place, that is usually enough.
The threshold is simple: Standard tops out at 50 users. If headcount reaches 55 in six months you will have to move to Professional, so plan the licence a year ahead, not around today's team.
Count everyone who will log in to the portal: not just sales reps but managers, accounts, the warehouse and assistants. A common mistake is to size the plan by the sales team and then find that the whole company wants tasks and chats.
### We will pick the right plan for your team
Tell us how many people will use the portal and which processes you need: we send a plan recommendation and an AED setup estimate

## Professional is about automation, not headcount
Professional is AED 731 a month billed annually and holds up to 100 users. This is where the plan list first shows sales automation, call tracking, email marketing, ad automation, booking, analytics and reporting tools, task time tracking, task automation, RPA, HR tools and 1 TB of storage.
A team of 25 needs Professional when the process runs on automated scenarios: deals move through stages on their own, calls are tied to ad sources, the manager reads funnel reports. Which of your scenarios work on Standard is something we test on a demo portal before you buy, not after.
Enterprise starts at 250 users and AED 1,465 a month billed annually. Its list adds unlimited branch accounts, central administration, multi-level permissions, Active Directory integration and login history. For a team of up to 100 it is usually more than you need.
## Annual billing saves about a third
Billed monthly, Standard is AED 529 ($144) and Professional AED 1,061 ($289). Billed annually, Standard comes to AED 4,368 a year against AED 6,348 monthly, a difference of AED 1,980 or about 31%. Once a team has decided on Bitrix24, paying for the year is almost always the better deal.
The vendor price page also lists Vibe+ versions of the plans with extended AI features and REST API access, priced higher than the regular ones. Whether you need them depends on your tasks: a standard sales CRM usually does not.
## The licence is not the whole cost of a CRM
The plan is paid to the vendor, while setting the portal up around your process is the partner's job. At MakeBiz Technologies a standard CRM setup starts at AED 10,000, work beyond the standard is AED 200 an hour and connecting WhatsApp is AED 500. ## A worked example: a company grows from 12 to 60 people
A hypothetical distributor in Sharjah starts with 12 users on Standard: AED 4,368 a year for the licence. A year later it has 60 people, the Standard cap is exceeded, and it moves to Professional at AED 8,772 a year.
